articles.title: Eli Manning says Arch will have to 'figure out' media, learn when to 'relax'
articles.summary: Eli Manning had some pointed words for his nephew Arch after the Holly Rowe situation, says Arch needs to be "careful."
articles.body:
Much has been made of the much more succinct Arch Manning that showed up ahead of Texas' matchup with Tennessee . But to Eli Manning, it's part of the business.

After Arch made headlines following Texas' win over Ohio State for his comments about an AI-generated video of Texas coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe, he issued a public apology that Rowe then publicly accepted, thus seemingly burying the hatchet.

According to Arch's uncle, those are just the kinds of situations Arch needs to learn to navigate on his own.

"Most of my advice, more football stuff," Manning told Front Office Sports. "He'll have to figure out that media on his own, and a lot of it is just kind of growing pains. You feel like they're your pal, you relax with them a little bit, you try to be funny, and then they can take it and run. So you just got to be careful. You got to find your moments where you can be funny, you can be relaxed, but there's certain things that you know you just got to learn and deal with it. And I think he has learned, and he apologized and did the right steps in handling that."

Arch's demeanor in press this week was notably different, perhaps as a bit or perhaps as a correction. He kept his answers short and football related, declining to comment on extraneous topics.

The opponent, of course, might play into that. The Vols are a different team to prepare for than UTSA, so he may be focused on the week at hand. Either way, if any family has media experience, it's the Mannings.

articles.title: Martina Navratilova joins WNBA controversy after Olympic champion demands answers on the league’s definition of ‘woman’
articles.summary: Martina Navratilova has added her voice to a growing dispute over how the WNBA defines eligibility for its women’s league.
articles.body: Martina Navratilova has added her voice to a growing dispute over how the WNBA defines eligibility for its women’s league. The tennis legend publicly backed former Olympic swimmer Nancy Hogshead, who has launched a petition asking the WNBA to clearly define who qualifies as a woman. Hogshead’s campaign has drawn support from several former athletes and public figures and has collected more than 21,000 signatures, according to The Daily Signal. The issue has gained fresh attention as women’s sports continue to debate how leagues should handle transgender athlete participation and establish eligibility rules.Why is Martina Navratilova backing Nancy Hogshead’s WNBA petition?Navratilova’s support came after Hogshead, a three-time Olympic gold medalist from the 1984 Los Angeles Games, launched a Change.org petition calling on the WNBA to define “woman” as female. Hogshead has argued that the league needs a clearer standard for eligibility rather than relying on a broad statement that only women can play.Navratilova shared a Daily Signal report about the petition on X and wrote: “3-Time Olympic Gold Medalist Launches Petition Demanding the WNBA Define What a Woman Is – The Daily Signal- well done Nancy!!!”Hogshead’s argument is rooted in her own experience as an elite swimmer and her later work as a civil rights attorney. She said she underwent sex verification as an athlete and believes sports bodies should set clear eligibility standards.The petition also has backing from former professional basketball players Charles Barkley and Enes Kanter Freedom, while Lara Trump has publicly supported the effort. The campaign followed a letter from several Republican members of Congress, led by Rep. Marlin Stutzman, asking the WNBA to clarify its definition.What does the WNBA controversy mean for women’s sports?The central dispute is not simply about one player or one game. It is about how a professional women’s league defines its competitive category and what standards should determine eligibility.The WNBA says only women are eligible to play, but the current debate centers on the absence of a more specific public definition, according to the reports behind the petition. Hogshead wants the league to establish a rule that she says would protect the female category.The question has become more visible following comments from WNBA player Sophie Cunningham about transgender participation in women’s sports. Those remarks triggered criticism and support, adding another layer to an already heated discussion around fairness, inclusion and eligibility. Reuters reported in August that sports organizations have been revisiting policies for transgender participation, with different groups emphasizing competitive fairness or concerns about exclusion.For now, the WNBA eligibility debate remains unresolved. articles.title: Beyond the spotlight: How Cristiano Ronaldo's wife Georgina Rodríguez quietly built her own activewear brand, Mimoa
articles.summary: Georgina Rodríguez has spent years living under one of the biggest spotlights in sport, but her latest move puts the attention somewhere else.
articles.body: Georgina Rodríguez has spent years living under one of the biggest spotlights in sport, but her latest move puts the attention somewhere else. The model, entrepreneur and longtime partner of Cristiano Ronaldo has launched Mimoa, an activewear and lifestyle label built around comfort, movement and everyday life. Rather than making the brand simply another celebrity fashion project, Rodríguez has positioned Mimoa around a clear idea: women should feel comfortable in what they wear without feeling pressured to change their bodies. That message now sits at the centre of her growing business identity.Georgina Rodríguez turns her fashion experience into MimoaRodríguez's move into activewear did not come out of nowhere. Long before Mimoa, fashion had become a major part of her public identity.Her career began far from the world of celebrity campaigns. Vogue Arabia reported that Rodríguez worked as a shop assistant at Gucci in Madrid in 2016, around the time her life changed dramatically after meeting Ronaldo. As her profile grew, so did her relationship with fashion. She later appeared in Vogue editions and worked with major names including Chopard, Charlotte Tilbury, Guess and Moncler.That experience gave her something many celebrity-founded brands struggle to build: a personal connection with clothing.Mimoa takes that experience into a category Rodríguez knows from her own lifestyle. The brand describes itself as a premium activewear and lifestyle label designed for women who move between different parts of their day. A workout might be followed by school runs, errands, meetings or dinner. Mimoa aims to fit into all of those moments instead of treating exercise as the only reason to wear active clothing.That distinction is important.The modern activewear market has moved far beyond gym clothes. Leggings, fitted tops, sweatshirts and sports jackets now sit comfortably alongside everyday wardrobes. Mimoa is entering that space with the idea that one outfit can follow a woman through several parts of her day.Mimoa puts comfort at the centre of its activewearThe strongest part of Mimoa's identity is its message around comfort.The brand's official story says its pieces are created to move with the body rather than against it. Rodríguez has also described the thinking behind the label in deeply personal terms."I created Mimoa from a feeling, that a woman's body is not something to fix."That sentence explains much of the brand's direction.Instead of selling activewear as a tool for achieving a different body, Mimoa presents clothing as something that should work with the body a woman already has. Its official philosophy focuses on softness, stretch, fit and ease, with the body itself treated as the starting point for design.That is a notable change from some traditional fitness marketing, which often links sportswear with transformation. Mimoa takes a different route. Its language is less about correcting flaws and more about making clothing feel natural.The brand's FAQ makes a similar point. Mimoa says it is designed for women who want performance and everyday wear to exist together, while also placing femininity and comfort on equal footing.That positioning gives Rodríguez a clear space in a crowded market.She is not trying to compete only on technical sportswear. She is selling a lifestyle.Georgina Rodríguez's Mimoa collection goes beyond the gymMimoa's current range reflects that wider approach.The official store features tops, sports bras, leggings, shorts, hoodies, sweatshirts and other pieces that can be combined into full looks. Its collections include names such as Your Flow, Your Classics and Your Form, giving the range a more fashion-led identity than a traditional sports uniform.The colour choices also support the everyday focus. Alongside black and grey, the brand offers softer and brighter options across different collections. Some pieces are designed to be worn as sets, while others can work as separate wardrobe staples.Current listings show items such as striped straight leggings, zip jackets, hoodies, Bermuda sweatshorts and seamless T-shirts. Prices vary by market, with European listings showing pieces from around €39 to €69 and US listings displaying selected items at prices such as $55 and $97.That product mix reveals something about the business strategy.Mimoa does not appear to be built around a single viral item. Instead, Rodríguez is developing a wardrobe that can cover different situations. A woman might wear leggings for a workout, a zip jacket for travel or a sweatshirt for a casual day out.The result is closer to an everyday lifestyle collection than a narrow gymwear label.Georgina Rodríguez is building an identity beyond RonaldoPerhaps the most interesting part of Mimoa is not the clothes themselves. It is what the brand says about Rodríguez's career.Being connected to Cristiano Ronaldo has placed her in a unique position. Her relationship with one of football's biggest stars brought enormous attention, but Rodríguez has spent years developing a public identity of her own.Vogue Arabia noted that she deliberately worked to establish an image beyond being known simply as Ronaldo's partner. That effort has included her Netflix series I Am Georgina, fashion work, brand collaborations and major public appearances.Mimoa fits naturally into that progression.There is a difference between appearing in a campaign and owning the idea behind a brand. With Mimoa, Rodríguez is presented not only as its face but as its founder. The company's own website places her name and philosophy at the centre of its story.That gives the project a more personal foundation.Her lifestyle also makes activewear a believable category. Rodríguez has spoken about a daily routine built around family, children, the gym and life on the move. Her public image has long included fashion and fitness, so Mimoa connects several parts of the persona she has already developed.The bigger challenge now is turning that personal following into a lasting fashion business.Celebrity can create attention. It cannot, by itself, guarantee repeat customers.Mimoa will ultimately have to earn those customers through fit, quality, comfort, design and consistency. Its current strategy suggests Rodríguez understands that. The brand is not relying solely on her name. It is trying to establish a point of view.That may be the most important part of Mimoa's story.Georgina Rodríguez already knows what it feels like to be watched. With Mimoa, she is attempting something different: creating something people can choose for themselves.The spotlight may have helped open the door, but the clothes will have to keep it open.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Nurideen Shahid Shabazz, better known as Deen the Great, has built a name across boxing and social media. The American fighter first gained attention through videos featuring street fights, boxing challenges, comedy and confrontational content.His online popularity eventually helped him enter the influencer-boxing scene. Deen became the first fighter signed by Happy Punch Promotions before joining Misfits Boxing. He went on to win the promotion’s lightweight championship and became one of its better-known fighters. Outside the ring, he expanded into YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and livestreaming, building a large audience along the way.What is Deen the Great’s net worth in 2026? Deen the Great has an estimated net worth of $2 million (according to celebrity net worth). His income comes from several sources, including boxing, YouTube, livestreaming, sponsorships, appearances and social-media promotions.His boxing career remains an important part of his earnings. Deen made his Misfits debut against Evil Hero in August 2022 and stopped him. He then faced Walid Sharks in November 2022 and rallied to score a third-round stoppage. The win earned him the Misfits lightweight championship.Deen later defeated Sharks again by unanimous decision in October 2023. He also stopped Dave Fogarty in August 2024 to defend his title. The championship reign eventually ended after the promotion stripped him of the belt following failed negotiations over a mandatory defence.His first recorded crossover-boxing loss came against Amado Vargas in December 2025. Vargas, the son of former world champion Fernando Vargas, won by unanimous decision over six rounds.Publicly reported figures include $50,000 linked to his 2023 fight with Sharks and $25,000 connected to his 2024 bout against Fogarty. However, boxing is only one part of his business.Deen has also built a major YouTube following. His channel has generated hundreds of millions of views, with his content moving from homemade fight videos to boxing, comedy, lifestyle content, collaborations and livestream highlights.His journey began around late 2019 and early 2020. After losing a low-paying job, Deen became interested in content creation. He experimented with several formats before finding success through fight videos.Deen’s social-media presence later grew across Instagram, TikTok and Kick. His Instagram following passed one million, while his Kick account grew rapidly through IRL streams, boxing discussions, collaborations and marathon broadcasts.His partnership with figures such as Adrien Broner also helped him expand his content beyond his own fights.Deen’s confrontational personality has also generated controversy. He has been involved in several public altercations and has exchanged heated words with other fighters.In May 2026, he was arrested in Miami Beach following an altercation involving a woman on a yacht. He pleaded not guilty. His attorney disputed the allegations.Despite the controversies, Deen has continued building his career across multiple platforms. articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: 5 players Hayden Winks is higher and lower on than consensus
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks highlights some players from the Week 3 rankings that deserve to be scrutinized.
articles.body:
Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks shares the players he's higher — and lower — on than Yahoo consensus for Week 3.

These rankings will be tinkered all the way until kickoff, so please check back in on our weekly rankings pages and Sunday AM sit/start show for the absolute latest.

These blurbs are also Hayden's The Blueprint, which are his weekly rankings and analysis column. T he RB version is out on Wednesdays , while the WR version and the QB/TE/K/DEF version are each out on Thursdays before Thursday Night Football.

Terrance Ferguson, TE, Rams — 49.5 proj. yards

Ferguson was unleashed in Week 2 without Puka Nacua. His role wasn't even that bad in Week 1 either, when he ran a route on 49% of Matthew Stafford dropbacks. But Week 2 was a totally different ballgame (71% routes) as a real featured player (30% targets and 13.0 expected half PPR points). Ferguson surpassed Colby Parkinson in 11-personnel, and he was a stand up slot player on a bulk of those snaps. When the Rams went heavy, Ferguson was often 1-of-2 Rams eligibles running a real route with a third option in the flats as a checkdown. Those are very valuable looks, as they often are tied with play action. Ferguson also had a target where he split through the B gap and caught a TD on a coverage bust in the end zone.

Those three drops were killer and a sign that he's an inexperienced player in development, but Ferguson is a must-hold for a long time at this point, even if Nacua returns in Week 3. The upside is too obvious. Without Nacua, Ferguson has a case to be a top-5 fantasy option. With Nacua, he's more of a dart throw. I'd treat him as a real target off the waiver wire if available. I hope you guys had him rostered from the draft or directly after Nacua went to DNP on Friday. Signs were here.

Jaylen Warren, RB, Steelers — 86.5 proj. total yards

Warren has outplayed Rico Dowdle in each phase to start the year. The pass protection difference is night and day, with Dowdle making critical errors multiple times in each game. Warren is also the better receiver in general. And the eye test and numbers suggest Warren has been more effective on the ground, too. Warren's -1% rush yards over expected are much better than Dowdle's -47%.

More importantly to that is the Dowdle toe injury. He left the game, returned and then was ruled out. Without Dowdle on the field, Warren played 50-of-52 snaps, only losing two to special-teamer Travis Homer. The Steelers offense is beyond disorganized right now, but there is potential for real bellcow usage if Dowdle misses. With Dowdle, Warren is the RB31 on RB20 usage. Dowdle was still in a walking boot on Wednesday. This assumes he is out.

Jameson Williams, WR, Lions — 54.5 proj. receiving yards

The Jameson Williams rollercoaster is a bumpy road, but he will play so much better than he has in the two games to start the year. He will have fewer layup targets with Sam LaPorta healthy, yet Williams' WR28 expected half PPR points are enough to keep the faith that the averages will warrant a weekly WR3 ranking. That just means living with a couple of WR5 outings before WR1 nirvana.

This is an eruption spot. The Lions are at home, projected for 27.0 points (fifth most), and host a secondary that doesn't have reliable outside corners. The Jets allowed 4-41-1 to Christian Watson last week and had multiple downfield DPI calls against Matthew Golden. Both are great comparisons for Williams' skill set.

Deebo Samuel Sr., WR, 49ers — 38.5 proj. receiving yards

The Niners are using Samuel just as they always have. He's mustered up a 22% target share with a lowly 3.3 average depth of target. He's had screens, backfield usage, a carry, quick outs of play action, and the occasional intermediate target in both games as a near full-time player. San Francisco also lost WR3/4 Demarcus Robinson in Week 2, and Mike Evans (hip) is at least on the injury report with a minor issue. With San Francisco looking as potent as ever, this is a real fantasy football role to chase. Samuel is the WR26 on WR33 usage so far. There's not a "washed" component to his film right now while he's at full health.

Rashod Bateman, WR, Ravens — 43.5 proj. receiving yards

We nailed the call last week (WR10 on WR17 usage), and Zay Flowers (hamstring) isn't practicing again. The reality is the rest of the Ravens' skill group is so bad that there's no choice but to get Bateman more involved. He is a former first-round pick for what it's worth. He's not a total scrub on tape.

The matchup is also excellent. The Cowboys had coverage busts against the Giants, lost multiple starters in the back seven since then, and also allowed wide-open explosive opportunities to Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs on tape last week. I'm not threatened by Daron Bland, and CB2 Cobie Durant (hamstring) is also looking doubtful to play. It's easy to make the math work when the Ravens are projected for 28.0 points, like they are here at home.

Tyler Warren, TE, Colts — 46.5 proj. yards

Six-of-seven targets to Warren last week were at or behind the line of scrimmage. His other one was the Chiefs' coverage bust that led to a wide-open TD in the middle of the end zone. It's not ideal, but it'll get the job done and absolutely gives him a better floor than others in this tier. Without Alec Pierce (heel) for the next month or longer, the Colts offense will feel very congested, but that also likely means an extra target or so to Warren. He's the TE13 on TE9 usage so far, as a more low-end TE1 than "elite" TE1.

Bucky Irving, RB, Buccaneers — 76.5 proj. total yards

Since 2024, the Vikings are sixth-best against fantasy RBs. They've only allowed five RBs to reach 20+ half PPR points; two of those were Jahmyr Gibbs. Their swarm style prevents RBs from getting into the route, and it could incentivize more snaps out of Kenneth Gainwell this time around. Minnesota has also added EDGE Dallas Turner and DT Jalen Redmond full breakouts to the equation this season. Over the last four games dating back to last year, Minnesota is the very best fantasy RB defense, allowing just 11.4 half PPR points to the entire room.

D'Andre Swift, RB, Bears — 86.5 proj. total yards

Swift can't be viewed as the RB1 he's scored like to open the year without Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion). The Bears only project for 18.5 points (29th) against an Eagles defense that has been very good since DC Vic Fangio showed up. The Bears will continue rotating drives between Swift and Kyle Monangai, and now it's for an offense that we don't love. Here is how many half PPR points Swift has scored when the Bears finished with 21 points or fewer since 2025: 9.0, 5.3, 9.7, 14.1, 14.4, and 12.4. That's an average of 10.8, equivalent to the RB23 on a per-game basis.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots — 53.5 proj. total yards

Week 2 was a major win for Henderson. Rhamondre Stevenson started the game, but he fumbled the ball in a nonsense yards-after-the-catch moment shortly after. The Patriots rode Henderson for a larger-than-normal split afterwards. He started the second half and ended with 16 carries to Stevenson's 6.

Henderson split between new LG Alijah Vera-Tucker and switched-position C Jared Wilson for a nearly untouched rushing TD, but the rest of the game was forgettable. He wasn't targeted or tasked with a single pass-protection rep, and the Patriots had 0 plays within the 5-yard line. We head into Week 3 without major answers of what the split will be. I'd lean Henderson as the touch leader, with Stevenson still the favorite for goal-line reps. It's worth noting that the Patriots have only averaged 16.7 expected half PPR points to their RB room through two weeks (27th).

Since Week 10 of last year, the Jaguars have allowed 60 yards per game to RBs, easily the best mark in the NFL.

Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders — 42.5 proj. receiving yards

McLaurin was sadly inches away from a very big fantasy outing in Week 2. He had three targets in the end zone that went incomplete (including on a flea flicker) and a ticky-tack OPI called on him on a slant win. Only accumulating 6.0 half PPR points on 15.4 expected points is a real bummer, especially knowing we're getting Marcus Mariota now.

McLaurin has 10 games with Mariota attempting more than 10 pass attempts (most of these were starts). He has averaged 12.1 half PPR points (WR12) on WR15 usage and an 18% target share, leading to 104 air yards per game. Mariota has been more aggressive in recent years, and it's possible McLaurin can hold onto some fantasy relevance as we head into bye weeks. Those numbers are the absolute best outcome, however. The difference is the presence of Stefon Diggs, who is playing in a mini Amon-Ra St. Brown role under new OC David Blough. Diggs has a slightly higher target share through two weeks, 23% to 20%.

The Seahawks are the second-best fantasy WR defense when adjusting for schedule since Week 10 of last year. They'll have elite CB1 Devon Witherspoon in McLaurin's general area, and I don't trust these backup offensive linemen with all of the funky things Seattle does defensively.

articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 9: D Gukesh channels his world champion self, overturns almost-lost game to keep India in gold hunt
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.How Gukesh turned the tables on DonchenkoPlaying black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications. It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.Vantika, Divya lead India's women to victoryIndia's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either. articles.title: Los Angeles Sparks fire coach Lynne Roberts after the team again misses the playoffs
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Sparks fired coach Lynne Roberts on Friday, a day after her team missed the playoffs for the second straight year under her leadership.  Robe...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Sparks fired coach Lynne Roberts on Friday, a day after her team missed the playoffs for the second straight year under her leadership.

Roberts was hired in 2024 and the Sparks went 37-51 in her two seasons in charge of the team.

"We are grateful to Lynne for the commitment and determination she brought to the role, which was evident all the way through our last game last night" Sparks special advisor Farhan Zaidi said. "Lynne has cared deeply about our organization and for our players and their development. We sincerely thank her for everything she has invested in the Sparks and wish her and her family the best moving forward."

The Sparks had a solid squad coming into this season with Kelsey Plum and Nneka Ogwumike leading the way along with Cameron Brink . Plum was hurt in the early part of the season and then traded to Phoenix. Ogwumike was solid all year long, but announced this would be her last season playing in the WNBA and retired after Thursday's loss to Golden State.

The Sparks will rebuild around Brink and two potential lottery draft picks. The team has a new general manager in Ariana Andonian, who was hired last month to replace Raegan Pebley.

Speaking Thursday about her time in Los Angeles, Roberts said: "I think we've had two tough years of injuries, and I'm not trying to blame anything on that, it's just the reality. There has been a lot of change. Our president's been here ... four months. So just again, so much change."

articles.title: Sparks news: How Nneka Ogwumike’s final act of accountability sums up HOF career
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – When the dust had cleared and the sting from the Los Angeles Sparks’ heartbreaking 76-75 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the season final...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – When the dust had cleared and the sting from the Los Angeles Sparks ' heartbreaking 76-75 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the season finale had settled down a bit, Nneka Oguwmike stood before the home crowd and took accountability .

The Sparks had held a double digit lead for most of the night, and seemed well on their way to ending the year on a high note against one of the best teams in the league. But the Valkyries battled back and surged ahead late in the fourth quarter. A fourth quarter that saw Ogwumike miss a put-back at the rim that could have won the game. She also missed a crucial free-throw that, given the final score, could have made a world of difference.

Now those plays aren't the sole reason the Sparks lost, far from it. But on a night when late-game officiating came into question and a night when Nneka Ogwumike was being celebrated as she heads into retirement, she took the mic and apologized to the Sparks' home crowd for missing the shot and missing the free-throw.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

She still allowed herself to enjoy the festivities and to revel in the jubilee, but she wouldn't be who she is without taking responsibility.

"I think that's just the competitor in me. I think I'm really big on it. I talk a lot about discipline and grinding through with grace. I'm still thinking about how I missed that free-throw," Ogwumike said during her postgame press conference, the final one of her career. "I know it might be silly because we're not playing in the postseason, but it's just how I like to play. And having that level of accountability is important. I think it's how it makes us better. I think it's what keeps us hungry, it keeps us driving. It keeps me wanting to be dangerously disciplined and just to be great."

The fourth quarter was filled with plenty of mistakes, many of which were equally as crucial as the two Ogwumike plays. The Sparks suffered breakdown after breakdown defensively, including the most egregious in the final seconds, helping off the strong side corner and allowing Valkyries All-Star wing Gabby Williams to get a wide-open 3-point shot that put them ahead.

But when Ogwumike's teammates heard her take ownership for the game's outcome, it wasn't a shock to them. That's the person they've come to know and love, and it would have been surprising to them if she didn't do that.

"I think that's just a testament to just who she is," Rae Burrell said during her postgame press conference. "That consistency, she's able to take accountability, but also just that moment to thank all the fans and the people around that have helped her, help us get to this point. She's just very thoughtful in that sense too. Just making sure that she thanked everybody in the speech … it was great."

Ogwumike finished her last WNBA game with 17 points, 15 rebounds, five assists and one steal in a game-high 35 minutes. She remained on the court long after the final buzzer sounded, long after her postgame speech, allowing teammates, family, fans and everyone else one last moment to appreciate and celebrate her presence.

And as the Sparks now head into uncharted waters with a future that is less certain than it was just a few months ago, Ogwumike hopes she can continue to be an example for a franchise that from top to bottom, would do well to follow her lead.

"I don't think I'll ever change in that way. And I hope that people understand that that's just the standard that I hold myself to," Ogwumike said. "And I'm grateful that, of course, people are showing love and support regardless. But hopefully me holding myself accountable is also something that we can carry on as we look to really turn this organization around."

articles.title: Rangers £15k-A-Week Signing Emerges as Kris Boyd’s Standout Summer Pick: Can They Build Around Him?
articles.summary: Rangers have started to see the benefits of their summer rebuild, with Kris Boyd identifying Dan Neil as the standout arrival. Speaking to Seven, powered by...
articles.body:
Rangers have started to see the benefits of their summer rebuild, with Kris Boyd identifying Dan Neil as the standout arrival. Speaking to Seven, powered by Ladbrokes, Boyd said several new players had taken time to settle but had recently shown much stronger form.

Neil joined Rangers from Sunderland on a free transfer in July and signed a three-year contract. The 24-year-old has since taken on the captain's armband, while his influence has grown during Rangers' improved domestic run.

Boyd pointed towards the team's defensive improvement and greater competition for places. He named James Penrice and goalkeeper Ivor Pandur alongside Neil as recruits who have impressed him. Neil then produced his biggest moment yet in the 3-0 League Cup win over Celtic at Ibrox on September 13, scoring twice as Rangers reached the semi-finals.

That result came before another Old Firm victory at Celtic Park. Ryan Naderi scored in the 1-0 win on September 20, while Pandur made a crucial save and Makhanya had a goal ruled out. Rangers therefore claimed two derby wins within eight days.

Boyd, however, raised a wider issue. He argued that Rangers cannot keep rebuilding at the same rate and must eventually give a settled squad time to develop together.

"It was exactly the same last season, and they've already moved a lot of last year's arrivals on, so the key sooner or later has to be stability. You can't keep chopping and changing players at the rate Rangers have been doing in recent transfer windows.

"I've got to be honest, I think at the start of the season, a lot of people were questioning a lot of the new signings.

"But it might just have taken a while for them to settle, and over the last three, four or five games, I've seen a lot of good things.

"Defensively, Rangers look really solid; I think that's maybe six clean sheets in seven now. They look strong, and there's competition for places which is absolutely key.

"You need someone breathing down your neck if you're playing for a successful team. If you've got that, you're going to perform better in training and that usually leads to better performances on the pitch.

"That's where Derek McInnes is at right now; he's now settled on a team and he'll be hoping he can build on that.

"Dan Neil has been excellent since he's come in; he ran the show at Ibrox and he's one I'm really looking forward to seeing more of this season.

"The majority of signings have impressed me to be honest… James Penrice is another one.

"The goalkeeper [Ivor Pandur] looks like he's been Rangers' goalkeeper for a number of years already… he looks pretty safe.

"I'm sure Derek will feel there are still names that can do a lot more, but the most important thing for me is the competition for places."

Can Rangers build their next team around Neil?

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – SEPTEMBER 20: Dan Neil of Rangers controls the ball during the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Glasgow Rangers at Celtic Park on September 20, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

I agree with Boyd's central point, although Neil's value goes beyond his goals against Celtic. Rangers needed more control in midfield, and Neil has increasingly provided it while giving McInnes another reliable organiser in the middle.

His leadership matters too. Sunderland had already trusted him with the captaincy, and Rangers have handed him the armband during a period of major change. That experience can help a team carrying several new faces.

The two goals against Celtic added the obvious headline. Yet his bigger contribution comes from his positioning, passing and willingness to protect the defence. Those qualities give Penrice greater freedom to attack, particularly when Rangers push numbers forward.

Makhanya deserves plenty of credit as well. His performances against Celtic have made him one of the most visible new arrivals, while his defensive work has helped Rangers maintain their improved structure. Still, a central midfielder can influence more phases of a match.

Pandur has strengthened that platform from behind. Rangers started the season with plenty of questions, but recent results have brought a different feel. The side kept St Mirren, Motherwell and Aberdeen out before beating Celtic twice.

That sequence gives McInnes something valuable, and that's selection pressure. Penrice can challenge others, Pandur looks increasingly secure, and Neil has become difficult to leave out.

Boyd's warning about squad churn therefore deserves serious attention. Rangers cannot keep replacing large sections of the team and expect instant cohesion. Neil arrived for nothing, yet his leadership and recent influence make him look like one of the most consequential pieces of McInnes' rebuild.

For Rangers, keeping this core together may matter as much as finding the next signing.

articles.title: Video: Norma Dumont throws condoms, money at Ailin Perez during UFC Vegas 121 faceoff

Norma Dumont vs. Ailin Perez was elevated to the co-main event of Saturday's UFC Vegas 121 at the Meta APEX, and the bantamweight contenders continued their pre-fight verbal war at the staredown.

Dumont and Perez made weight Friday morning, and moments later, stood face to face in front of the cameras for the final time, both carrying their country's flags. When Perez did her traditional twerk, Dumont threw condoms at her.

"You need this," Dumont said with a smile.

While Perez was picking it up on the floor, Dumont threw money at her.

"You pay whore with money," Dumont said. "Take it, it's yours."

Both fighters discussed their personal feud earlier this week in interviews with MMA Fighting, promising to follow it all up with an intense fight.

"She's already not someone who has much shame about anything, neither in her personal life nor anything else," Dumont said, "so now that the contract is signed, I already have my date to beat her, I have my time to do what I need to do, what I want to do without getting arrested, so it makes absolutely no difference to me what she does outside of the fight."

"Her weakness, everyone says it's the ground," Perez said , "because she doesn't get up, because she has heavy hips and can't move… No, her biggest weakness is her mind, and that's where I'm going to work, I'm going to get inside her head. I'm already winning the fight, you know?"

"My team is saying I'm going to knock her out, I want to finish her, I want to put Norma to sleep."

articles.title: Paul Skenes Gives Brutally Honest Truth About Pirates Season
articles.summary: After his final start of the season, Skenes addressed his feelings regarding missing out on the playoffs in 2026.
articles.body:
The Pirates entered the 2026 season with the belief that they could make the playoffs, so falling short of the postseason picture will be considered a disappointment by many.

Among those who are disappointed is Paul Skenes , who closed his season with a 3.82 ERA in 32 games. It was a significant step back for Skenes, as he produced stellar ERAs under 2.00 in each of the last two seasons, which is only exacerbated by the team missing the playoffs once again.

Skenes believed the Pirates had a chance to contend for at least a wild card spot in 2026, but the team will instead finish third in the division. While that is the team's best NL Central finish in a decade, Skenes wanted to get his first taste of October baseball this fall.

After his final start of the season, Skenes addressed his feelings regarding missing out on the playoffs in 2026. Here's what he had to say.

Skenes had a solid close to his season on Thursday, allowing just one run in 6.1 innings as the Pirates beat the Cardinals. The win guaranteed the Pirates won't have a losing season this year, but the team had playoff goals that it won't fulfill when the regular season concludes.

After the game, Skenes discussed the Pirates not making the playoffs once again, and the star pitcher expressed that he was over ending the season so soon.

"It's tough. This is my third year and every year at the end it's been like, 'what's it going to look like for next year?'" he said. "I don't love that. I'm kind of tired of it."

However, Skenes did say he likes where the team is at moving forward and believes that the right moves in the offseason can help take the Pirates to the next level.

"We are in a good position for next year, I know that," he said. "But it's going to be tough to think like that again for the whole offseason...I don't think there's anything that needs to be completely overhauled."

By reaching the 80-win mark, the Pirates secured their best season since 2018, when they went 82-79. If Pittsburgh can get to 83 wins this weekend against the Tigers, it would be their most successful season since they last made the playoffs in 2015.

Still, the incremental improvements weren't enough to reach the postseason, and with three years left on Skenes' contract, the clock is ticking for Pittsburgh to return to the playoffs.

Washington RB Brian Bonner Jr. breaks out against Minnesota

Bonner drew praise throughout fall camp and was heralded as the next multi-year starting RB for the Huskies. Of course, nobody expected his time as a starter would begin so quickly, but then Quaid Carr and Jayden Limar went down with long-term injuries in the same game, opening the door for Bonner to take over. I think Bonner posts his first 100+ yard game and scores his first collegiate touchdown with Washington comfortably beating Minnesota at home. — Froton

Cooper Barkate announces his presence in Miami

After destroying the ACC with QB Darian Mensah for the conference champion Duke Blue Devils , Barkate followed Mensah to South Beach in hopes of elevating his game and challenging for a national championship. While the numbers haven't been elite, averaging 8.2 half-PPR points per game, Barkate has run the second-most routes on the team (67), just slightly behind superstar WR Malachi Toney (71).

With Miami's WR3 Joshua Moore out of the season, and Toney deemed questionable to play against a lower-echelon CMU secondary that ranks 115th in pass success rate allowed (47%), I think Barkate is finally featured and clears 100+ receiving yards with a touchdown against the Chippewas. — Froton

articles.title: Keys to victory for the Oregon Ducks vs. USC Trojans
articles.summary: Three keys for the Oregon Ducks to score a massive rivalry victory on the road against the USC Trojans.
articles.body:
This one has been circled on the calendar for both programs since they met last November. The rivalry between the Oregon Ducks and USC Trojans is well documented , and it's only grown to be more intense in recent years as the Ducks have consistently been part of the national picture, while pressure mounts on the Trojans to make the playoff field.

Dan Lanning and Lincoln Riley have plenty on the line this week, in terms of their future program success and in terms of this season. Dante Moore and Jayden Maiava were both tremendous in this game last season, and plenty of points are expected to come from their offenses again this weekend. Both offenses will be without key weapons , including Jeremiah McClellan for Oregon and Trent Mosley and Corey Simms for USC, but that doesn't dilute the firepower that will hit the field on Saturday.

The defenses are another story. The Trojans surrendered 35 points to lowly Rutgers last week, and 30 points to Louisiana the week prior. Oregon was torn apart on the road by Oklahoma State because of a lack of discipline at the line of scrimmage, and the Ducks played from behind throughout. If the Ducks are playing catch-up in Los Angeles again this weekend, it could be a long day.

However, I do think there are more ways for Oregon to win this game than there are for USC. The Ducks have been tested more than the Trojans, and the Ducks have plenty of depth to work with across the field. There are a few areas where the Ducks need to win to get their season back on track. Let's take a look at three keys to help Oregon score a massive rivalry victory against USC on Saturday night.

This was a key last week, and the Ducks did a good job. Obviously, USC is going to be a tougher opponent defensively this week than Portland State was last week. Still, Oregon needs to run the ball on early downs and stay in short-yardage spots on second and third down. Last season, that's exactly what the Ducks did.

Oregon lived in short-yardage spots in this game last season and converted on 7-of-12 third-down attempts. Dante Moore was able to open up the play-action game in short yardage, and part of that was because of the threat Jordon Davison posed on downs with a distance of three yards or less.

The Ducks haven't run the ball well this season, and USC's front seven is much improved. I trust USC's defensive line to generate pressure, but I don't trust the depth on the defensive line or at linebacker as the game goes on. If Oregon can run the ball early, the gaps will only get bigger late in the game.

I think this game could follow a similar script to last season's game, where Moore has plenty of success throwing the ball for big gains because the Ducks can keep the Trojans off balance in short-yardage situations. The offensive line struggled on the road earlier this season, particularly at tackle, but if the Ducks play in short-yardage situations, that will influence how USC chooses to rush the passer. If the Ducks are also hitting on short passes early on, threat neutralized.

There are plenty of ways for Oregon to win this game, particularly on offense. The Ducks have not been in good situations on third down often this season, and that is the make-or-break down in this matchup. Penalties and a lack of execution on first down held the Ducks to just 34.6% on third downs against Boise State and Oklahoma State. Oregon has preached improving its discipline and leadership since the loss, and this is the opportunity to prove there is some merit to that by staying ahead of the chains.

Both offensively and defensively, the biggest factor in this game for Oregon might be out wide. The Ducks have been more pass-happy to start the season, and their defense has also been shredded through the air. I expect USC to attack the secondary like the Trojans did last season in this matchup, and Oregon should do so as well.

The Trojans' secondary is banged up, with Alex Graham and Jontez Williams both potentially playing with injuries. Dakorien Moore and Evan Stewart are going to be leaned on by Dante Moore , and the Ducks need to win in their routes early. Being physical as a receiver often comes with size, but Stewart has a track record of winning jump balls downfield, and Moore is a threat to beat any corner off the line of scrimmage with his feet. Offensively, that's where the Ducks need to win.

On defense, the Ducks can't be afraid of USC taking shots downfield. USC has young receivers that will be facing a higher level of competition for the first time, and this is a big prove-it game for Brandon Finney Jr. , who struggled in this game last season. The Ducks directed a lot of attention to Makai Lemon last season, and Tanook Hines had a breakout game against the Oregon secondary. Finney, in particular, struggled with penalties and was beat for jump balls on the sideline.

I need to see Finney, who might play more out of the nickel this week, step up and prevent USC's receivers from getting on their line at the snap. The same goes for Ify Obidegwu , who had an interception in this game last season, and Na'eem Offord on the perimeter. Oregon has played plenty of zone this season, but I think the Ducks can win in man this week if they are aggressive at the line of scrimmage and knock the Trojans around.

This is also a big game for Koi Perich and Aaron Flowers to play responsibly on the back end, because USC is going to take its shots. But the Trojans haven't faced much adversity this season and a physical defense. Oregon has the opportunity to set the tone early. The Ducks have committed more than their fair share of penalties this season, so the Trojans will want to expose that, but Oregon has a chance to flip the script if they can play physical at the line and get their heads turned around on the back shoulder throws.

It's a rivalry game. Lanning noted this week that this is "not just another game," despite what some players and coaches, even Moore, would want you to believe. There is a lot on the line for both teams and the future of each program in terms of their dominance of the recruiting area in Southern California. Lanning and Riley are both facing pressure to win for some of the same and some different reasons.

The Ducks panicked on the road against Oklahoma State when things weren't going their way. That can't happen against a USC offense that is built for a track meet. This is a game where it can be easy for one player to think they need to be Superman and win the game on their own. That's where teams fail to execute, relying only on instinct and not what they have prepared for by watching film and practicing throughout the week.

Oregon has to show growth this week to signal that the potential many saw for the program this season is still alive. Linebackers can't overpursue in the run game. Edge rushers need to read the option. The offensive line can't have pre-snap penalites and needs to get to the second level. No dropped passes. Simply put, just do your job.

Both rosters are very talented, but Oregon has more depth at each position to keep up if this game gets wild and high-scoring. USC doesn't have the depth up front defensively, so if Oregon can execute well, then the end of the game could be its to lose. Don't get swept up in the stakes of the game and the rivalry itself. If Oregon is truly the better team, it should execute accordingly. Play loose and play free.

articles.title: Roger Federer explains why he thinks Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner both got injured this year
articles.summary: The ATP Tour has not been the same this year, and the reason why is simple: the absence of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner. Their...
articles.body:
The ATP Tour has not been the same this year, and the reason why is simple: the absence of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

Their respective injury issues resulted in three missed Grand Slams between them, has drawn questions over the relative strength of the men's game at the minute, given the lack of players who have stepped up.

Only Alexander Zverev seems to have really taken advantage, having finally ended his career-long major title hoodoo.

Many have pointed to the ever-increasing tennis schedule as the main reason for these and many other injuries this year, with Alcaraz complaining about the gruelling schedule once again recently.

However, speaking to Sky Sports, Roger Federer has posed another theory.

Roger Federer discusses Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's injuries this year

Asked how he managed to keep fit in light of injuries to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner , and for his thoughts on their lengthy lay-offs, he admitted: "I mean I feel like it's a bit part of the game."

Federer then added, recalling experience gained during his own incredibly long career: "I mean, I think back in my career, in 2013 I didn't win a title, in 2016 I didn't win a title because of injuries, and we talk about, yeah, I was always there. Yeah, I was always there, but you have your ups and downs; you're fighting with some sort of an issue, and they had it maybe a little bit this year, but still they won both a Slam, both had a tremendous year regardless, so for me it was: when I look at the long runway, how do I keep longevity going and what are my goals, and then you work back from that.

'I think that helped me a lot. Of course, as a team it's like understanding how much you're playing, when to play, with whom to train, where to train. There's so many little details and then, let's be honest, sometimes you're just also unlucky. All of a sudden something hurts, you didn't realise it was that serious, and then you've got to just sit it out. I think maybe that's what happened with the guys a little bit this year."

This comes not long after Federer claimed Sinner has still had a better year than Zverev , despite recent arguments.

articles.title: Bucs rookie making an immediate impact
articles.summary: Ted Hurst has quickly carved out a role in Tampa Bay's offense, and Sports Illustrated believes bigger plays could be coming for the rookie.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven't found much to celebrate during their 0-2 start, but the early development of rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III has provided at least one encouraging sign.

Sports Illustrated's Justin Melo included Hurst among five rookie wide receivers making an immediate impact entering Week 3. The third-round pick hasn't put up huge numbers yet, but his usage through two games suggests Tampa Bay is already comfortable giving him opportunities within the offense.

Hurst has five receptions for 63 yards through his first two NFL games. He caught three passes for 36 yards against Cincinnati in Week 1 before adding two receptions for 27 yards in Tampa Bay's 23-19 loss to Cleveland. The Buccaneers' official statistics confirm those totals.

The numbers only tell part of the story. Hurst was targeted seven times against Cleveland, and Sports Illustrated noted that those opportunities came with an average depth of target of 23.1 yards. Melo also pointed out that Tampa Bay has moved the rookie around, with 40 snaps coming outside and another 20 from the slot through two games.

That usage is noteworthy for a player only two games into his NFL career. Tampa Bay selected Hurst out of Georgia State with the No. 84 overall pick in April, making him the Bucs' first offensive selection of the 2026 draft. His combination of size and speed was a major part of what attracted Tampa Bay to him, and the Bucs have wasted little time trying to put those traits to use.

Hurst has already come close to producing the type of downfield play Sports Illustrated believes could eventually become a bigger part of his game. Tampa Bay took multiple shots in his direction against Cleveland, including a crucial opportunity during the Bucs' final possession.

With Tampa Bay trailing by four in the closing seconds, Baker Mayfield delivered a pass to Hurst in the end zone. The ball reached the rookie's hands, but with a defender tight in coverage and heavy rain coming down, Hurst couldn't complete the catch. The Bucs eventually turned the ball over on downs and fell to 0-2.

Mayfield didn't sound discouraged afterward. He said Hurst remains a player he trusts and made it clear that one missed opportunity isn't going to stop him from looking in the rookie's direction moving forward.

That's the most encouraging part of Hurst's start. Five catches for 63 yards isn't going to jump off the page, but a rookie receiver earning 10 targets through his first two games while being used as a legitimate downfield option is worth paying attention to.

There will still be growing pains. Hurst has caught only half of his targets, and the Bucs need some of those near misses downfield to turn into completions eventually. Sports Illustrated's inclusion of him among the rookie receivers already making an impact speaks more to the role he's earned and the opportunities Tampa Bay is giving him than raw production alone.ng place to start. Hurst has already earned Mayfield's trust and a meaningful place in Tampa Bay's offense. The next step is turning those opportunities into the explosive plays the Bucs drafted him to make.

articles.title: Top Texas school forfeits wins after transfer QB from Oklahoma ruled ineligible
articles.summary: The Fighting Farmers' perfect start disappeared just as the top-ranked program prepared to begin district competition.
articles.body:
One of Texas' top-ranked high school football programs has just seen its undefeated record wiped out.

The Lewisville Fighting Farmers , the No. 13-ranked team in the state by Rivals , started their season with three consecutive wins against non-district opponents. However, according to Matt Stepp of Dave Campbell's Texas Football , the District 5-6A Executive Committee (DEC) ruled on Friday that Lewisville used an ineligible player and must forfeit its victories.

Why Lewisville must forfeit its first three wins

Laykon Brassfield, a standout junior quarterback for the Fighting Farmers, transferred from Edmond North in Oklahoma to the North Texas school after his sophomore year. According to Stepp, the DEC's investigation found that Brassfield did not actually reside in Lewisville, which makes him ineligible for varsity competition for one calendar year from the date he enrolled in the high school.

"The 5-6A DEC ruled that he did not meet the UIL [University Interscholastic League] criteria for a bona fide residence in Lewisville ISD or at Lewisville HS," said Greg Riddle of the Dallas Morning News after the ruling.

Lewisville is expected to appeal the DEC's 7-0 ruling in favor of forfeiting the games to the UIL State Executive Committee, hoping to secure a waiver for Brassfield's family and relocation. According to Riddle, the DEC also decided 5-2 that Brassfield did not move for athletic purposes.

What the forfeits mean for Lewisville's playoff chances

The Fighting Farmers had big wins over three respected programs in Dallas Highland Park, Trophy Club Byron Nelson and Denton Ryan. Brassfield, a rising top recruit in the state, tallied 734 passing yards and 14 passing touchdowns along with 133 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns.

It's unclear whether Brassfield will be able to play Friday, but senior quarterback Aiden Enriquez is currently tabbed as next up on the Fighting Farmers depth chart.

Because all three forfeited games were against non-district opponents, the ruling does not directly damage Lewisville's District 5-6A record or its route to the playoffs. But Brassfield's immediate ineligibility could have a far greater effect as Lewisville begins district play Friday against rival Marcus in a Battle of the Axe rivalry game.

articles.title: Bills get shaky 'game-time' injury updates on DJ Moore, Keon Coleman for Week 3
articles.summary: These two Bills receivers have an uncertain status for Week 3.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are 2-0 to begin the 2026 season, with wins over the Houston Texans in Week 1 and the Detroit Lions in Week 2. Now, heading into Week 3 against the 0-2 Los Angeles Chargers , Josh Allen is eyeing a 3-0 start to the season.

Unfortunately, he might not be operating with a full-strength offense. While the running back and tight end rooms aren't in question, there is a lot of uncertainty at wide receiver.

On Friday, a few days before Sunday's big matchup, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network shared that the Bills will have both WR's DJ Moore and Keon Coleman questionable for Week 3, with both being "game-time" decisions, putting their status in doubt.

Bills' DJ Moore and Keon Coleman are 'game-time' decisions for Week 3

"Bills listing WRs DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) as questionable, with Joe Brady telling reporters he'll give them until game time Sunday vs. the Chargers. Same with DT Ed Oliver (hip)," Garafolo reports.

This injury update on Coleman and Moore is a significant one, as both Bills wide receivers are questionable for Week 3 against the Chargers.

But it's much more than simply being questionable. They're both game-time decisions, which is one step between being questionable and doubtful.

The shoulder injury for Moore could keep him out a week, and the same goes for Coleman's ankle injury.

While they could both play in Week 3, there is a chance they both are ruled out and sit for a week to be as close to 100% as possible for their next game.

If both sit, Khalil Shakir , Josh Palmer , and Skyler Bell will see the bulk of the work at wide receiver, with there likely to be plenty of Dalton Kincaid , Dawson Knox , and James Cook III as well.

Moore and Coleman are questionable, game-time decisions for the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. For now, it's a shaky situation that won't have a resolution until the "game-time" decision is made.

articles.title: Gotta do it the hard way: Phillies vs. Rays series preview
articles.summary: Three games, magic number: Two. Let the fun begin.
articles.body:
The Phillies could have made this easier on themselves. Instead, they find themselves fighting for their playoff lives, possibly needing to win two games against the best team in the American League.

The good news is that the Rays don't need to win these games and may be more interested in resting players and getting lesser-used relief pitchers some work. On the other hand, it's the Phillies. They haven't done anything the easy way all season, so why start now?

I understand why some Phillies fans want to trade every prospect. It's been a while since a Phillies' prospect – especially a position player – has panned out and become more than a decent at best major league player. That doesn't happen to other teams, especially it seems, the Rays. For instance, Junior Caminero was a top five prospect in baseball a few years ago, and at age 23, he's completing his second straight 40+ home run season.

For a second, it looked like Caminero's season might have been ruined due to his appearance at the All-Star Game.

That comes after another hit by pitch in the WBC.

I guess the guy is a magnet for baseballs in exhibition games?

I suppose Caminero has slowed down somewhat post-injury. He "only" has an .818 OPS with 13 home runs in the second half as opposed to .929 and 28 in the first. Sounds like he could use a break, and if the Rays want to give him a couple of days off this weekend, I wouldn't complain.

I can't hate the Rays too much. After all, the greatest moment I've experienced as a Phillies fan came in a game against them.

But I will repeat endlessly that Major League Baseball in Florida does not work. You can blame crappy stadiums or crappy ownership, but the fans rarely support the team even in the best years. For instance, this season, the Rays have the best record in the American League, but the third worst attendance in baseball. And sadly, this is one of their best years attendance-wise!

They're going to build the team a new stadium, and I can't see this turning out much differently than how it went for the Marlins after they got a new stadium in 2012. Fans might go the first season or two, and then attendance will return to near the bottom of baseball.

Let's hope that the Phillies can build up their minor league system in the next few years so that when Caminero inevitably goes on the trade block, they can be in the mix.

The weather might play havoc with the games this weekend. That probably isn't great for the Phillies, but if you're fighting for a playoff spot on the final weekend, then that's what you have to deal with! Had the Phillies not sucked earlier in the season or given away who knows how many winnable games, they wouldn't be facing must win games now.

They may need to use Zack Wheeler on Sunday which would eliminate him from being used in the Wild Card series. It will be curious to see if they'll use him and the four seed – and homefield advantage – is on the line Sunday. I would not, because I think Zack Wheeler gives them a far better chance of winning than Citizens Bank Park would.

It would be great if the Phillies could just get everything wrapped up on Friday night. Then we can sit back and watch two bullpen games with mild bemusement instead of existential dread. Will the Phillies actually make it that easy on us? Probably not!

My guess is that they put up double digit runs in one of the games and win easily, while scoring three runs combined in the others. Will that be enough to make the postseason field? Probably, but they will make us sweat it out.

articles.title: Flyers forward Trevor Zegras slapped with one of the most ridiculous penalties of all time
articles.summary: Trevor Zegras was sent to the penalty box for tucking his jersey into his pants during the Philadelphia Flyers' preseason win over the Boston Bruins.
articles.body: The NHL is still working through its preseason, and already we have a candidate for the worst penalty of the year, and possibly ever. The Philadelphia Flyers hosted the Boston Bruins in their penultimate tune-up before their season-opener against their arch-rivals, the Pittsburgh Penguins. Now, the Broad Street Bullies came out on top in this one, 2-0, but that wasn't the story. Instead, all of the talk after the game had to do with Flyers forward Trevor Zegras getting a minor for delay of game for "improperly wearing equipment." MLB TELLS UMPIRE DOUG EDDINGS HE MADE A MISTAKE IN DEMANDING CARDINALS PITCHER STRAIGHTEN HIS HAT Zegras hopped over the boards to take a faceoff with the back of his jersey tucked into his pants. Most of us wouldn't think twice about it, but an official saw it and sent him to the sin bin. That's because this season, officials have been told to crack down on players not wearing equipment properly, and technically, he was. But that doesn't make it any less absurd. MASSACHUSETTS YOUTH HOCKEY PLAYER SUSPENDED AFTER VICIOUS SLASHING INCIDENT GOES VIRAL At the risk of sounding like a certain cartoon sports radio host, it used to be that tucking your sweater into your pants was the cool thing to do. Well, not anymore. According to The Athletic, Zegras confirmed after the game that he had been issued a warning before he was given the penalty, which is in line with the rulebook. Had he done it again, it would've been a game misconduct. Head coach Rick Tocchet mentioned afterward that the league had given a heads-up about this push — which focuses on everything from visors to neck guards to, of course, jerseys — a few weeks earlier. "They told us, in all fairness, two, three weeks ago," Tocchet said. "I didn’t even think about it. … Obviously, can’t do it anymore. Regular season starts, we can’t have a penalty like that. I actually had to put (forward Matvei Michkov’s jersey) down on the bench." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hey, rules are rules... but nothing says preseason like the league picking a rule that never gets enforced to the point that most of us forgot it existed, and then dropping the hammer.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Penta at Money in the Bank, Sami Zayn vs. Kevin Owens Finish, Worlds Collide
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Penta Reportedly Considered Internal MITB Favorite

Following his impressive performance in a World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns on Raw in Mexico City, Penta reportedly may be the wrestler to beat in the men's Money in the Bank ladder match.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), Penta is viewed internally as the "heavy favorite" to win MITB and earn an opportunity to challenge for a world title at a time and place of his choosing.

WWE reportedly did not originally plan to have Penta win Money in the Bank, but the outlook may have changed following his match against Reigns.

Penta reportedly impressed WWE decision-makers with the viewership numbers and merchandise sales that came along with his match against Reigns, leading to the belief that WWE could go back to Penta vs. Reigns at some point despite the original plan for it to be a one-and-done bout.

Since making his WWE debut on the Jan. 13, 2025, episode of Raw, Penta has established himself as one of the most popular Superstars in WWE.

He had an impressive Intercontinental Championship run already, and if he prevails at Money in the Bank, it will mark the biggest win of his WWE career to date.

Penta already qualified for Money in the Bank by virtue of his win over Dominik Mysterio and Dragon Lee on Monday, and he very well may be the man to beat at MITB.

Details on What Went Wrong with Zayn vs. Owens Finish

A referee error was reportedly to blame for the awkward finish to the WWE Championship match between Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens last week on SmackDown.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), referee Ryan Tran took the blame for how the finish transpired, and there was backstage "heat" on Tran because of it.

Tran reportedly said he got confused, but he is considered a "very credible" official.

In the closing moments of the Zayn vs. Owens title bout, CM Punk interfered by hitting KO with the WWE Championship belt.

Zayn pinned Owens after Punk's interference, but the referee did not count to three and Owens did not kick out in a timely manner, making it clear that there was some kind of miscommunication.

Owens and Zayn did their best to save it, as Zayn hit KO with his signature Helluva Kick right after and pinned him to win the match and retain the title.

While the mixup took away from an otherwise strong SmackDown main event, both Zayn and Owens are popular and talented enough to move past it and make the most out of the situation moving forward.

WWE's Reported Broadcast Plans for Worlds Collide

Despite going head-to-head with AEW's All Out pay-per-view in Chicago on Saturday, the WWE Worlds Collide event is reportedly not expected to air live.

According to False Finish , a WWE source said back in July that the plan was for Worlds Collide to stream live on YouTube, however, Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp , PWInsider.com and Meltzer have all since reported that there were no longer plans for the show to be streamed live.

The initial source False Finish spoke with followed up and reportedly said they were "unsure" why WWE reversed course, as WWE planned as recently as two weeks ago to being announcers into Chicago for Worlds Collide.

Thursday on Something to Wrestle (h/t WrestlePurists ), AAA announcer and WWE Hall of Famer JBL said he and the other announcers were not being brought in for Worlds Collide, noting that he believed the revised plan was for them to commentate over the show in post production.

Meltzer (h/t WrestlePurists ) reportedly Friday that there is speculation within WWE regarding Worlds Collide being exclusive to Club WWE subscribers.

However, Meltzer added that it hasn't yet been confirmed that Club WWE will be the ultimate landing spot for Worlds Collide.

During WWE's recent live event tour of South America, Stephanie Vaquer won the Women's World Championship in her home country of Chile, beating Liv Morgan.

WWE later announced that the match can be watched exclusively as part of the Club WWE subscription service.

If Worlds Collide follows suit, it would signal WWE's strong desire to funnel its fans toward Club WWE for certain premium content.

articles.title: Italy crisis deepens as Belgium’s win stalls World Cup rebuild in Rome
articles.summary: Belgium win 2-0 in Italy as Nations League opener is played out in front of nearly half empty Stadio Olimpico.
articles.body:
Six months on from failing to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup, four-time champion Italy is still struggling.

Italy was beaten 2-0 at home by World Cup quarterfinalist Belgium in the Nations League on Friday in the Azzurri’s first match since a playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March.

Roberto Mancini marked his return to Italy’s bench three years after he abandoned the job for a lucrative deal to coach Saudi Arabia, and he appeared frustrated on the touchline.

By contrast, it was a successful debut for new Belgium coach Mark van Bommel, the former Netherlands international who was hired when Rudi Garcia left after the World Cup.

Only 47,155 spectators showed up in the 70,000-seat Stadio Olimpico and the home fans were already whistling 20 minutes in after Mika Godts put the visitors ahead with his first international goal.

Dodi Lukebakio doubled Belgium’s advantage midway through the second half.

Kevin De Bruyne — making his 125th international appearance — set up Godts on the left flank, and the Belgium number 10 cut inside and dribbled past three defenders before slotting past goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Godts, who recently joined Paris Saint-Germain, turned defender Gianluca Mancini the wrong way, and his fellow centre-back Diego Coppola came sliding in too late.

Coppola was playing in place of Alessandro Bastoni, who was suspended after being sent off in the loss to Bosnia.

The counterattack began with a poor pass from midfielder Alessandro Romano, who was making his Italy debut after switching international allegiance from Switzerland.

Belgium’s second also came on a counterattack as Lukebakio scored from beyond the area after midfielder Sandro Tonali ran back in a desperate effort to stop him.

Mancini’s starting lineup contained eight players who had featured regularly during the World Cup qualifying campaign.

The 61-year-old Mancini led the Azzurri to the European Championship title in 2021, but shockingly resigned as Italy coach in August 2023, taking over Saudi Arabia’s national team two weeks later.

It will not get any easier for Italy, who visit Turkiye on Monday and then go to France next Friday, before hosting Turkiye in Bologna to conclude the first phase of Nations League matches.
