articles.title: Warrington Wolves through to Super League Grand Final after controversial penalty with 14-12 win over Leeds Rhinos
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves are into the Grand Final for the first time since 2018; The two points came from a penalty for an escort on George Williams; The play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continue through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3
articles.body:
It marks Warrington's first Grand Final since 2018 and they have never been victors in the big dance before. Leeds, meanwhile, are left waiting once again, with their last Grand Final victory coming all the way back in 2017.

The flashpoint of the match came in the 66th minute when James McDonnell was pinged for an escort on George Williams. It appeared as though Williams had potentially run into the Leeds man's line, but despite the Rhinos using their Captain's Challenge the decision was upheld and Ewan Irwin sent over the conversion to win the game.

Remarkably, with no time remaining on the clock, Jake Connor attempted to send over a penalty for Leeds from 62 metres out to level the game but could not get enough power on it.

The game was level at 12-12 at the break in what was an enthralling contest. Leeds Rhinos had got onto the scoreboard through converted tries from Ryan Hall and Jake Connor, while Warrington had gone over through James Bentley and Luke Yates.

Warrington will find out their opponent for the Grand Final on Saturday when Wigan Warriors host Wakefield Trinity, live on Sky Sports , with kick-off at 5.30pm.

The Super League Grand Final then takes place on Saturday October 3, with kick-off at 6pm, live on Sky Sports .

Penalty the difference as Warrington into big dance for first time since 2018

The strategies of both teams became clear early on. Leeds, rocked by the losses of backs Lachie Miller, Maika Sivo, Ash Handley and Jack Bird, put their emphasis through the middle, relying on their pack to win the attritional battle.

Meanwhile, Warrington put their focus on an aerial bombardment of Hall at the end of their sets. That paid dividends as early as the fifth minute when Matty Ashton out-jumped the try-scoring legend and found Toby King, who passed in field to Bentley for the former Rhino to open the scoring.

But Leeds would hit back 12 minutes later. Hall would get the better of Ashton this time as the Warrington flier made a defensive misread and slipped, giving Hall the space to score from Brodie Croft's cut-out pass.

Warrington wasted a gilt-edged chance soon after, with Albert Hopoate unable to ground a Williams grubber despite having no Leeds defenders around him.

The Rhinos punished them within minutes. It was a try crafted and finished by Connor. The current Man of Steel kicked over the Warrington defence, Ned McCormack got there first, passed to Kallum Watkins, who drew the last defender and put Connor away for a score. His two conversions gave Leeds a 12-6 lead.

That, however, was nullified before the break. Williams' flat pass found Luke Yates, who wriggled out of Cooper Jenkins' grasp to score by the sticks. Irwin's second goal put the game level at half-time.

The second half was an attritional battle, with neither side giving an inch. They both made errors with the ball but were unrelenting in defence.

The breakthrough eventually came, in controversial circumstances. McDonnell was adjudged to have taken out Williams while chasing a kick, albeit it appeared harsh. Leeds' Captain's Challenge was unsuccessful and Irwin slotted over the penalty for a two-point lead.

The drama wasn't over though. While Warrington handled the closing period well, there were moments. Connor thought he'd come up with a clutch 40/20 out of nothing, only for Warrington to successfully overturn the call as Keenan Palasia had offloaded after the tackle was completed.

Then, with the final play of the game, Leeds received a penalty, and Connor opted to go for two to level the game from 62 metres out.

Headingley held its breath, but his kick fell short, allowing Warrington to kick the ball dead and secure their passage to Old Trafford.

Just 12 months earlier in the play-offs St Helens had a penalty from 60 metres out with no time remaining but opted to kick to touch and stunned Leeds with their 'Left to Wright' finish. The Rhinos will never know if they could have done the same.

Arthur: That penalty call should not deciding game of this magnitude | Burgess: There's nothing to celebrate about yet

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur to Sky Sports:

"It's a tough loss. I'm extremely proud of the boys.

"Everything that could go wrong probably did this week. But we didn't use it as an excuse.

"We fought really hard, and I'm really disappointed. I feel like the game has been decided by a really tough penalty.

"That penalty should not be deciding a game of that magnitude.

"There was plenty of fight, but in the end it wasn't enough. The only thing we could control was our attitude, and ours was excellent.

"We didn't want it to end this way. It would have been nice to let the two teams decide the result I reckon."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess to Sky Sports:

"There's nothing to celebrate about yet.

"It's out of our hands in that moment [Connor's penalty], so what was going to be was going to be.

"I'd composed myself either way. You've got to save the emotion.

"I was nervous, and I wanted us to experience this as a group together, getting to the final week of the season.

"We want to enjoy this week and make the most of it. And get our best performance onto the field. We want to do eveyrthing that will help that."

Friday September 18: Wakefield Trinity 26-16 Leigh Leopards

Saturday September 19: Warrington Wolves 35-12 Hull KR

Semi-Final 1 - Friday September 25: Leeds Rhinos 12-14 Warrington Wolves

Semi-Final 2 - Saturday September 26: Wigan Warriors v Wakefield Trinity, 5.30pm KO on Sky Sports

The Super League play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continue all the way through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3.

articles.title: Warrington Wolves beat Leeds Rhinos to reach Super League Grand Final: Should the 'soft' penalty that decided semi-final have stood?
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur said the penalty that sent Warrington Wolves to the Super League Grand Final was 'soft'; watch Wigan Warriors vs Wakefield Trinity in the Super League semi-finals live on Sky Sports on Saturday September 26, with kick-off at 5.30pm
articles.body:
It started as expected with two big packs going at each other, the likes of Keenan Palasia and Ben Currie standing up for their sides as they have all season.

It hit the crunch point with 14 minutes remaining when James McDonnell was penalised for an escort on George Williams. In truth, it looked like Williams ran into the Leeds man's line, but even with a Captain's Challenge the decision was upheld.

That allowed Ewan Irwin to break the deadlock and send over the two points that sealed Warrington's spot in the Grand Final for the first time in eight years.

Whether it was a penalty or not will be debated and discussed. For Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthue it is not the type of decision that should be deciding a semi-final.

"It's a tough loss. I'm extremely proud of the boys," Arthur told Sky Sports .

"Everything that could go wrong probably did this week. But we didn't use it as an excuse.

"We fought really hard, and I'm really disappointed. I feel like the game has been decided by a really tough penalty.

"That penalty should not be deciding a game of that magnitude.

"There was plenty of fight, but in the end it wasn't enough. The only thing we could control was our attitude, and ours was excellent.

"We didn't want it to end this way. It would have been nice to let the two teams decide the result I reckon."

"I don't want McDonnell wearing that because he did nothing wrong," Arthur later added.

Was there even enough contact to knock Williams over? Most say no. What is agreed on is that Williams "played the game" and got the reward.

"I don't think strictly that is a penalty. I don't think it is," said Sky Sports Rugby League's Jon Wilkin.

"I think James McDonnell is running back, looking where the ball is going, in line with the ball.

"He's not aware of where George Williams is, but George Williams knows where McDonnell is, let me tell you that.

"It is just such a softie, and there's not enough contact to knock George over.

"George's biggest contribution tonight in a poor performance for him was that. It's smart, it's experienced, and it won his side two points.

"In a game like this, Brad Arthur is right to some extent that it was crucial. They [Leeds] also missed chances.

"But I am completely aligned with Brad Arthur that that isn't a 'penalty.'"

The fight referenced by Arthur was clear to see as the clock ticked down. Connor was trying for 40/20s and 20/40s all over the park.

He thought he had one with a minute on the clock but then Warrington used their Challenge and it was ruled that the tackle on Palasia was complete before he passed it off the ground.

Then, there were seconds remaining on the clock as Connor decided that he would try for the conversion from a penalty awarded. He was 62 metres out and it fell eight metres short.

It was the latest 'what if' moment for Leeds as they have to lick their wounds and go through another strong season with nothing to show for it.

Now, it is for Arthur and his squad to try and find a way to overcome controversy and rise once again.

That will not bother Warrington though, who are now 80 minutes from the biggest win in the club's history.

articles.title: Racehorse gets new name after concerns about reference to Hitler
articles.summary: LEXINGTON, Ky. — The Jockey Club has ruled that a racehorse known as Austrian Painter has been renamed Merrylegs after a review of a complaint that alleged it was a reference to Adolf Hitler.
articles.body: LEXINGTON, Ky. — The Jockey Club has ruled that a racehorse known as Austrian Painter has been renamed Merrylegs after a review of a complaint that alleged it was a reference to Adolf Hitler. The horse’s name drew attention after winning his debut Monday at Horseshoe Indianapolis Racecourse. Hitler was born in Austria and was an artist before becoming the head of the Nazi Party in Germany. “The Registrar determined that the name is ineligible under Rule 6.F.9.d, which prohibits names that ‘are likely to be offensive or threatening based upon factors including, but not limited to, color, creed, disability, ethnicity, gender, national origin, race, religion, politics or sexual orientation,’” the Jockey Club said in a statement announcing its decision. Owner and breeder Scott Herbertson said on social media it was a reference to Austrian painter Gustav Klimt and that his filly originally called New Order was named for his favorite band. New Order is also a term for the Nazis’ plan for occupying Europe. The Jockey Club said that horse, a full sister to Merrylegs, had also been unnamed. “We take these matters seriously and appreciate that they were brought to our attention,” the Jockey Club said.

articles.title: Juan Carlos Ferrero could return to coach Carlos Alcaraz next year, former world number one predicts
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz’s split with longtime coach Juan Carlos Ferrero late last year came as a huge shock to every tennis fan. In December 2025, Alcaraz...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz's split with longtime coach Juan Carlos Ferrero late last year came as a huge shock to every tennis fan.

In December 2025, Alcaraz and Ferrero parted ways , ending their incredibly successful player-coach relationship after seven years working together. Ferrero had guided his Spanish compatriot to six of his seven Grand Slam titles and mentored him en route to becoming the youngest world number one ever.

Alcaraz's former assistant coach, Samuel Lopez, assumed the role of head coach after Ferrero's departure. Under Lopez's wing, Alcaraz has since gone on to complete the career Grand Slam.

Dinara Safina predicts Juan Carlos Ferrero's future

Recently, Ferrero revealed he intends to return to coaching in 2027 with an unnamed player. Some have speculated that the player will be Alcaraz's rival, Jannik Sinner, while others think it might be 20-year-old star Rafael Jodar.

But former women's world number one, Dinara Safina, thinks Ferrero is going to reunite with Alcaraz in 2027.

As per Tennis 365 , Safina said: "For some reason, it tells me that he will come back with Alcaraz. I don't know, I could be wrong. They've talked about [Jannik] Sinner and a few others, but I don't think so. I don't believe [Rafael] Jódar either. But I insist, I could be wrong."

Asked by journalist James Grey about the rumours surrounding Ferrero, Alcaraz said: "I am really happy that he is coming back to the tour. See him around. It is going to be great. Whoever he is going to coach, I think the player is going to be great."

Sinner's current coach, Darren Cahill, was scheduled to leave the Italian's team at the end of the 2025 season, but decided to stay for one more year.

In an interview with Digisport earlier this year, Sinner said: "Darren is a very, very important part of our team. He keeps all the team very close, and with his experience, it's important, especially in moments where things don't go our way.

"He's important. We had a nice talk in the end of the year, last year, after the ATP Finals, and I tried to talk a bit in general. He made a move what went in my favour and it was an important move, that he can stay for one more year, which for me, it is very important in this moment and the stage where I am.

"So him, with the combination with Simone [Vagnozzi], it's a great combination. They know each other very well, they trust each other very well. So I think it has been very good."

With Cahill and Simone Vagnozzi in his corner this year, Sinner has won five ATP Masters 1000 tournaments and clinched his second Wimbledon title.

articles.summary: New York Giants great Eli Manning details his relationship with quarterback Jaxson Dart.
articles.body:
Eli Manning knows life without Jaxson Dart will be hard for the New York Giants .

The Giants raced out to an excellent start to the 2026 season, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 in Week 1. Dart was a big reason for that victory as he turned in arguably the best performance of his young NFL career, posting three touchdowns, no interceptions, and a 134.2 passer rating to go along with 54 rushing yards.

However, that feel-good moment was short-lived as the Giants' franchise quarterback suffered a season-ending knee injury during the first drive of their Week 2 loss against the Los Angeles Rams .

Manning, who is best known for leading the Giants to two Super Bowls, said he has a "good" relationship with Dart and texted him after the Cowboys game. He's always wishing for the best for Dart and the Giants.

"I sent him a text after the game last week, and thought he played outstanding," said Manning of Dart. "They threw a lot on his plate, and he was, you know, it seemed like he had great control of the offense. And it's a brand new offense; he's in his second year. It's not that easy, so I thought he did a great job. I feel like we have a good relationship, and you know, I think he knows I'm on his side and I want him to do well. I want the Giants to do well and right the ship."

With Dart sidelined for the entirety of the season, he'll be rehabbing and looking ahead to 2027. There is a slim chance that Dart could return for the playoffs if the Giants qualify. For the most part, Dart will be looking ahead to next season.

Prior to the game against the Rams, Manning said he's not someone who often texts players advice, but he gives it out whenever they ask.

"I'm not one of those that gives advice unless asked for advice, so it's more just a text of encouragement, a text of congratulations," said Manning. "Over the years or over the course of the season, I'll see him a few times in person. He may ask a question, how to deal with this, what to do, whatever it might be. What to do in an off week or how to handle this type of coach or how to handle this type of situation or a player. So happy to give advice when asked."

The Giants will have to move forward without Dart as they head into Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans with Jameis Winston at quarterback.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan on Nick Bosa's injury: I know he's bummed, but he'll be back
articles.summary: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice.
articles.body:
49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice.

"We can't say exactly, but I'm guessing around a few weeks ," Shanahan said of Bosa's timeline, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com.

The 49ers ruled out Bosa and rookie defensive end Romello Height (hand surgery) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. They have been hit hard by injuries in the defensive line.

Defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (foot) and defensive tackle Alfred Collins (patellar tendon) are on injured reserve. Rookie defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. has a high-ankle sprain that will keep him out multiple weeks.

"Losing Bosa was rough yesterday," Shanahan said. "I mean, losing six out of the 10 D-linemen in the last two weeks that have made our team is a little unusual. I don't think I've been a part of that, so that has been different."

Bosa returned from a torn ACL in his right knee and played 70 snaps over the first two games. He injured his knee in Week 3 last season, almost exactly a year ago, in a game against the Cardinals.

It is unclear whether Bosa injured his right calf, as Shanahan said he wasn't sure.

Bosa was warming up before the walkthrough when he injured his calf.

"I know he's bummed out, but he'll be back," Shanahan said.

The 49ers are still deciding whether to place Bosa on injured reserve. Only eight players can return from IR during the season, and the team already has several players on IR who it plans to return to the roster.

"He's right there at that point, along with a couple of other guys that are all in the same boat," Shanahan said. "Because of the number we have on [injured reserve], we won't be able to do all of them. So we've got to decide, and we're just trying to guess which ones will go longer, which ones have the chances of being sooner, and it's just a guess.

"They're all really in the same boat, so we've got to decide that by tomorrow."

articles.title: Cardinals Receive Bills Trade Pitch They Can’t Ignore for Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.summary: The idea of Marvin Harrison Jr. landing on the trade block by Week 3 felt unthinkable when the season started. But then, ESPN’s Dan Graziano dropped an updat...
articles.body:
The idea of Marvin Harrison Jr. landing on the trade block by Week 3 felt unthinkable when the season started. But then, ESPN's Dan Graziano dropped an update on Harrison Jr., and the rumor mill started working overtime for potential landing spots.

"Execs around the league are wondering whether the Arizona Cardinals could explore trading 2024 No. 4 pick Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline," Graziano wrote.

That alone was enough to spark the discussion on potential landing spots for the Cardinals wide receiver, and the latest one from Bleacher Report's Moe Moton has the Buffalo Bills as one.

Does Marvin Harrison Jr. to Bills Make Sense?

Most of the Super Bowl predictions have the Buffalo Bills as the Super Bowl favorite this season with the current roster they have. So, do they really need another wide receiver?

They already have a logjam in receiving corps with DJ Moore , Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman , and Joshua Palmer , and rookie fourth-rounder Skyler Bell. Adding another player just to tighten the competition wouldn't make sense.

"Still, with a Josh Allen -led offense, the Bills can make a work with the addition of another wideout," Moton writes. "In March, Bills general manager Brandon Beane traded a 2026 second-round pick to the Chicago Bears for Moore and a 2026 fifth-round pick. Keep in mind that Moore turned 29 in April and is coming off a down year, logging career lows in catches (50) and receiving yards (682) last season."

"Beane may be willing to offer the best trade package for Harrison, a 24-year-old receiver who hasn't reached his peak. The Bills can exercise the fifth-year option on his rookie deal to keep him under team control for two more years while they figure out where he fits in their offense."

Arizona Cardinals Pulling the Trigger a Long Shot, But Still a Possibility

Whether Beane would actually pull the trigger comes down to how they view the upside versus the ledger sheet. Moton says they have plenty of that in Harrison Jr.

Unless Keon Coleman breaks out this year, Harrison can be the new featured target on the perimeter opposite Moore, with Shakir in the slot. It would be a well-rounded group of receivers with Harrison as the potential long-term centerpiece."

It is all about the upside he brings, and one of the reasons he is the hottest name in the rumor mill entering Week 3 weekend is because the Cardinals are not seeing that upside this season.

Through the first two games, he's barely factored into the offense, pulling in just a single catch for 33 yards on four targets. After being drafted fourth overall to be the centerpiece, that kind of quiet stretch naturally gets people talking.

Arizona overly relying on Trey McBride and Michael Wilson might be partly to blame for why he's not performing well. Still, even in the grander scheme, Harrison Jr. is not performing the way everyone expected him to after a 62-catch for 885 yards and eight-touchdown season as a rookie.

A trade of this magnitude mid-season is a long shot. That said, if his production doesn't tick up soon, the noise won't stop anytime soon.

articles.title: OKC Thunder signs three more players to Exhibit 10 deals ahead of training camp
articles.summary: The OKC Thunder signed Andrew Holifield, Robert McCray V and Zhaire Smith to Exhibit-10 contracts on Friday.
articles.body:
The OKC Thunder signed Andrew Holifield, Robert McCray V and Zhaire Smith to Exhibit-10 contracts on Friday.

An Exhibit-10 contract is a one-year, non-guaranteed minimum salary deal. It'll allow all three players to participate in training camp, which begins Tuesday for OKC.

Holifield is a 6-foot-10 forward who went undrafted this past summer. He averaged 11.7 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.7 blocks last season as a senior at Lamar.

McCray is a 6-4 guard who also went undrafted this past summer after averaging 16.3 points, 6.1 assists and 1.3 steals as a senior at Florida State. And Smith is a 6-4 guard who was selected by the Philadelphia 76ers with the No. 16 pick in the 2018 draft. He averaged 20.9 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 33 games with the G League's OKC Blue last season.

OKC signed undrafted rookie Christop Tilly to an Exhibit-10 contract on Sept. 14 as well. They'll all compete at training camp in hopes of sticking with the Thunder, which still has an open standard roster spot .

articles.title: Yankees flop after CC Sabathia ceremony, lose to Orioles
articles.summary: Well, the pregame was nice at least.
articles.body:
With nothing left to play for on either side, the Yankees vs. Orioles series opener was somewhat overshadowed with the number retirement ceremony for CC Sabathia that took place before the game. The expected bad weather tomorrow forced a doubleheader today and moved the ceremony up to this afternoon as well. The short notice change led to the stands being emptier than anyone would like, but it was still a nice ceremony for the now-forever Yankees' No. 52. Old friends Derek Jeter , Andy Pettitte, Andy Pettitte, and Chris Young joined in the festivities on the field, alongside Sabathia's family.

On the field, things could've gone better.

Making something of a spot start with the doubleheader and the Yankees planning ahead for the postseason, Brendan Beck started for the Yankees. Not that it was something the Yankees were considering, but Beck didn't particularly make a case to be a last-second playoff roster addition. In his five innings, he allowed seven runs on six hits and three walks, including two home runs. The bullpen wasn't particularly lights out following him, allowing the Orioles to build up a big lead.

The Yankees' offense was always going to be up against it considering that fact, but they didn't do much. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers mostly kept the Yankees in check as Baltimore kept adding on. The Yankees could only plate one run from their eight hits, dooming them to a 10-2 loss in the first game of the doubleheader.

On the mound, Beck started things off with a couple scoreless innings. However, Baltimore got on the board in the third. Beck nearly got through the inning again, but issued a two-out walk to Dylan Beavers . That came back to haunt him, as Pete Alonso did a Pete Alonso thing and homered to put the O's in front.

An inning later, Beck loaded the bases after walking two and allowing a single. Christian Franklin then dropped in a single, plating another Orioles' run. After a force out got a runner at home, Beavers took Beck deep for a grand slam, putting Baltimore well in front.

The Yankees got on the board themselves in the bottom of the fourth. Heliot Ramos reached with a triple, aided by center fielder Colton Cowser misplaying the carom off the wall. Amed Rosario followed that with an easy single to score the Yankees' first run.

Baltimore got that run back a short time later, thanks to an outfield miscue of the Yankees' own. With reliever Yerry De los Santos in for the Yankees, Jeremiah Jackson hit a ball to deep right-center. The ball just got over the glove of Spencer Jones and took a fortuitous bounce past him. Jackson managed to race all the way around and beat the throw home for an inside-the-park homer, the first one in the Bronx in a dozen years — coincidentally with today's honoree on the mound against Wil Myers . Alonso added a more conventional homer in the seventh in that it went over the fence, but it was unconventional in that it was an absolute bomb, 471 feet away.

Honestly, I can't even be mad at that one. Baltimore would tack on one more run to get to double digits for the game. Paul Blackburn and David Bednar got their work in as expected, and we now won't see them again until the Wild Card Series.

The Yankees did get one run back after Spencer Jones singled in the bottom of the ninth and eventually came around to score on a Paul Goldschmidt sacrifice fly. Ben Rice struck out looking to end it.

One pretty disappointing thing to come out of the game was the play of the offense. Yes, the game didn't actually mean anything, but the Yankees did send out the likes of Goldschmidt and Rosario and their theoretical "lefty" lineup. Them not doing much on offense isn't what you would want to see considering that the Red Sox Wild Card Series lineup is now locked in and Boston has a bunch of left-handed pitchers they can throw at the Yankees.

The second game of today's doubleheader is set to begin at 7:30pm ET, which New York just announced. Brandon Young will go for Baltimore, while the Yankees will counter with Ryan Yarbrough , with Will Warren expected to provide relief work in anticipation of his playoff role.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s Moment Draws Love Amid Super Bowl Champ’s Apology
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, his second time suffering the injury in less...
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, his second time suffering the injury in less than a year. And the replay of his injury drew Tom Brady's profane reaction.

When the injury flashed back on screen, the seven-time Super Bowl champion didn't hold back, and his reaction has since gone viral online. By Thursday, he felt the need to address it publicly. Longtime teammate Rob Gronkowski is surprisingly defending Brady's raw reaction.

Rob Gronkowski Defends Tom Brady 's Unfiltered Call

Daniels originally dislocated his left elbow in Week 9 of the 2025 season against the Seattle Seahawks . The injury sidelined him for four weeks. Though he returned to the field in Week 14, he immediately re-injured the same elbow while trying to make a tackle, forcing the Commanders to shut him down for the remainder of his sophomore season.

Fast forward to Sunday's 37–20 loss against the Cowboys. The recurring injury caught Tom Brady completely off guard, prompting him to exclaim on the live microphone, "Oh sh*t. Excuse me, was not expecting to see that."

After the clip went viral online, Brady apologized on Thursday, saying, "I'm actually kind of embarrassed. There's a lot of grandmas at home that probably aren't very happy with my mouth on Fox. I'm gonna fix that. Sorry. I apologize."

Gronkowski, who played 11 seasons with Brady, told Front Office Sports that he disagreed with his former teammate's apology.

"It's a natural reaction, and that's what fans want," Gronkowski said . "I'd rather have him do that than be fabricated. Fans don't want fabrication. They want real, they want natural, and that was real and natural in the moment."

Gronkowski framed the slip as a sign of Brady's growing comfort in the broadcast booth, adding, "I'd say he holds back a little, because when he was playing, you were allowed to be intense and use those words. In the booth, you've got to be more appropriate, more buttoned up. So it was good to see him let loose, and it shows how comfortable he is now… He's killing it, he really is. I knew he'd start killing it sooner rather than later."

The slip adds to a growing list of raw on-air moments since Brady began his 10-year, $375 million broadcasting deal with Fox Sports. Later in the same game, his excitement got the better of him when he called a deep pass from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb an "absolute piss missile up the sideline."

Earlier in his broadcast tenure, he also drew attention online for a verbal stumble where he nearly blurted out a racial slur before quickly correcting himself to name Eagles lineman Landon Dickerson .

Meanwhile, Commanders coach Dan Quinn confirmed that initial imaging on Daniels' dislocated left elbow showed no fractures, though the signal-caller underwent more tests on Monday.

articles.title: Verlander's curtain call: What he's feeling and what it'll look like
articles.summary: Justin Verlander’s anxiety level was already climbing ahead of making the final start of his illustrious career.
articles.body:
DETROIT — Justin Verlander 's anxiety level was already climbing.

"High," he said. "It's weird. It's almost like a playoff anxiety."

The anxiety was hitting him on two levels. First, he was nervous about the ceremony that was planned to honor his career before the game Friday, Sept. 25. Nervous because he was being asked to give a speech.

But more than that, he was dealing with some early performance anxiety ahead of making the final start of his illustrious career on Saturday, Sept. 26.

"You always have anxiousness and nerves before you pitch," he said. "But in the playoffs, it's a different level. I haven't really known what to expect this whole time coming into this weekend. Yesterday and today, particularly today, I started really noticing like I'm really on edge right now. I have a lot of angst in a good way.

"I enjoy it, but I was like, 'Oh wow, this is more than maybe I anticipated.'"

Understandable. He hasn't pitched competitively since March 30. He's spent the last six months rehabbing from hip and hamstring injuries. Nobody knows what this might look like or how long it will last.

"I don't want to doubt him or put limits on him," manager AJ Hinch said. "We are going to give him as long a rope as he can handle, physically. As his injuries were mounting during the season, I thought this might be more of a cameo appearance. But the more I've talked to him, that's the exact opposite of what he wants. He wants it to be competitive.

"So, I don't know. It's hard to ask him to throw a normal set of pitches. But he's been doubted before and if he thinks he can handle it physically, I'm going to keep sending him out there and hope the right moment emerges. What inning is anybody's guess."

Hinch told Verlander that one thing was nonnegotiable.

"I told him, I'm coming to the mound and I'm coming to get you," Hinch said. "For old time's sake, if you want to scowl or yell at me or whatever, fine. His reaction was, 'You come out too early and we'll have our moment.' But he's not going to finish his outing. We are going to give him a sendoff that he is going to remember."

Pirates manager Don Kelly , one of Verlander's teammates in Detroit, joked that he was going to activate himself to get a couple of at-bats against Verlander.

"Hopefully he does," Hinch cracked. "We could use a couple of outs. But Donnie is not going to tell his guys to take."

Verlander wouldn't want it any other way. He's worked too hard, against all odds, really, for six months, to make this one moment happen. He wants it to be authentic.

"I'm sure you guys know I skipped a bunch of steps to be able to make the start," he said. "I mean, if we weren't home this last week, I don't know if I could have made it. It was that tight. Nobody really knows what to expect tomorrow. I don't know what to expect. AJ doesn't. It's kind of this gray area.

"But I've pushed as hard as I possibly can to be able to make this happen for me, for the fans, for Detroit."

One thing is for sure, he will leave the mound Saturday with no regrets.

"I feel like I ran my race," he said. "I've given everything I have. And plus, there are so many signs. I said I would pitch until the wheels fell off. Well, the wheel fell off. My kids at home. Like I see my daughter who's seven now, and how fast that goes, and how much of that time frame I've missed already.

"I have a 1-year-old son now, I know that I'm going to be able to be there for him and experience more of that childhood that I that I missed, unfortunately, with my daughter."

He thought for a second about regrets. He's won three Cy Young Awards, won an MVP award and two World Series rings. He's thrown three no-hitters. In terms of accolades and achievements, he's done it all.

"I think it's all how you look at it, right?" he said. "Like I could be sad that I didn't make the 300 wins. That was a goal. Damn, right? Listen, I'm not going to go home and lay my head on my pillow tomorrow night, no matter how the game goes, and be like I left something out there."

In the old days, Verlander would walk into the clubhouse Saturday, headphones on and in full snarl. There will be no headphones and certainly no snarl. He walked through the clubhouse Friday with a big smile and said, "Welcome to Justin Verlander day."

He credited the birth of his daughter Genevieve for that transformation.

"Once my daughter was born and I went away for COVID and had Tommy John surgery and got to spend so much time with her and the family, it just really changed me to the core," he said. "To the point that when I came back in 2022 and tried to go back into my old routine, it felt fake to me. So I started changing things. I would just use the love that she would give me.

"Honestly, I would leave for the park and there was this little girl and it didn't matter what I was going to do. It was just adoration and this bond that we had been creating. I'm not going to put my headphones on and be angry after that. I can't. It's impossible. So I just would use that energy, and it turned into one of the best seasons of my career."

There's a quote that Verlander has taken to heart.

"What's the point of living life if you don't let life change you?"

So it's on to the next life change for Justin Verlander. But first, there's Ver-fest at Comerica Park.

"I'm excited to see the atmosphere," he said. "I'm thankful for so many reasons. I didn't know if I was going to be able to make this happen physically, so to be able to do it makes me really thankful. And to have the city be so excited and abuzz about it makes me anticipate a good atmosphere, which I would love.

"I'm going to try to take in a little bit more and be a little more present than I than I normally am. Just try to have fun and get some guys out."

First pitch: 1:10 p.m. Saturday, Comerica Park, Detroit

TBD, Pirates: The Pirates have not announced their pitching plan.

RHP Justin Verlander (0-1, 12.27), Tigers: One more time, one last time. This will Verlander's 193rd regular-season start at Comerica Park, by far the most in any ballpark by any active pitcher. Aaron Nola is a distant second with 156 starts at Citizens Bank Park. And it's been a mere nine years and 37 days since Verlander last toed the rubber at Comerica wearing the Old English D (Aug. 20, 2017). It's also been 180 days since his last big-league start, which was March 30.

articles.title: Haaland’s brutal haircut jab leaves Man United fan waiting even longer
articles.summary: Haaland roasts Man United fan’s two-year no-haircut vow after City’s derby win keeps the challenge alive.
articles.body:
Football rivalries rarely need real drama to catch fire online. Sometimes all it genuinely takes is one cheeky comment, a viral personality, and a quite stubborn bet nobody expected to actually drag on this long.

Erling Haaland and self-styled superfan Frank Ilett now find themselves at the center of exactly that kind of spectacle. Their public back-and-forth has quickly spread well beyond typical football fan circles online.

Erling Haaland just added fresh fuel to one of football's strangest ongoing bets. The Manchester City striker told rival fan Frank Ilett to finally get a haircut, reigniting a viral challenge that refuses to end.

Ilett, known online as The United Strand, has spent nearly two years growing his hair out. He vowed never to trim it until Manchester United won five straight matches. Haaland decided that streak deserved mockery.

The exchange happened in the comments of a social post questioning whether Haaland's own haircut timing was a sly dig at United. Instead of staying quiet, the Norwegian jumped straight into the online debate himself.

Ilett officially started his unusual hair pledge on October 5, 2024. He promised United fans he would only visit a barber once the club strung together 5 consecutive wins.

What seemed like a realistic short-term goal quickly spiraled into a genuine internet phenomenon. United's inconsistent form meant Ilett kept growing his hair far longer than many fans expected.

By Sept. 26, 2026, Ilett had gone roughly 721 days without a haircut. His ever-growing hair became a running joke shared widely across football social media.

Fans speculated that Haaland's fresh haircut was a playful dig at Manchester United and Ilett's long-running no-haircut challenge. The theory quickly caught fire across football social media.

Ilett pushed back on that idea in the comment thread, arguing Haaland would have cut his hair right after beating United, not later against Sunderland after City's 5th league win.

Haaland responded directly and briefly, writing, "Cut your hair man," underneath Ilett's comment. The blunt reply spread quickly online, delighting City supporters and further fueling the rivalry between the fan bases.

Manchester City opened this Premier League season in dominant fashion, winning each of their first 5 league fixtures. That perfect run included a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Manchester United.

City stood alone at the top of the Premier League table after 5 rounds of fixtures. Their strong start helped fuel playful online jabs from rivals and fans.

Haaland debuted his fresh haircut on Aug. 23, the same day City's Premier League campaign began. Fans later connected the look to the ongoing playful exchange involving Ilett.

City's derby win over United arrived on Sept. 13, settled by Haaland's second-half goal in a 1-0 victory. That result kept United from building the kind of winning run Ilett needed to end his haircut challenge.

United have struggled for consistency, and this latest derby defeat added another frustrating result for supporters following Ilett's pledge.

Haaland has scored 9 goals in 11 Manchester derby appearances across all competitions. His latest goal in September further enhanced his derby record and gave City another victory in the rivalry.

Haaland's record against Manchester United has become a major part of the modern derby storyline. His September winner at Old Trafford added another chapter to a rivalry in which he has repeatedly delivered decisive moments.

The Haaland family history with Manchester United also runs deeper than haircuts and social media jokes. His father Alf-Inge was involved in a notorious 2001 clash with United captain Roy Keane, though the extent to which that tackle ended his career remains disputed.

United supporters have occasionally referenced Keane during heated derby moments, while Haaland has continued to answer on the field with goals.

Little-known fact: Haaland was born in Leeds , England, and plays internationally for Norway. Both of his parents are Norwegian, and he grew up in Norway.

The saga highlights how modern football rivalries increasingly play out online, through comment sections and quick replies, rather than only through matchday banners and stadium chants.

Ilett originally expected his challenge to last only 3 or 4 months when he started it in October 2024. Instead, United's uneven form turned the pledge into a long-running viral story.

Manchester City's U.S. social media account also previously joined the joke, posting an edited image of Haaland with long, flowing hair after United dropped points against West Ham .

Ilett's continued hair growth has made him look very different from how he looked when the challenge began, according to coverage of his viral transformation.

With United still searching for consistent form, Ilett's wait continues. Every dropped point keeps the challenge alive and gives rival supporters another reason to joke online.

The reverse Manchester derby is scheduled for March 2027, giving United another chance to shape the rivalry's narrative. Until then, Haaland's comment has ensured the haircut pledge remains part of the online conversation.

Ilett vowed on Oct. 5, 2024, to grow his hair until United won 5 straight matches.

Haaland told him, "Cut your hair man," after fans debated the timing of Haaland's own haircut.

City opened the league season with 5 straight wins, including a 1-0 derby win over United.

Haaland has scored 9 goals in 11 Manchester derby appearances across all competitions.

The challenge has passed 720 days as of Sept. 26, 2026, with no haircut yet.

articles.title: Browns' Todd Monken drops 'fired up' excuse to explain response to Mike Tomlin's remarks
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have taken many beatings over the years, both on the field and in the media. Regardless of who is manning the sidelines or taking snaps...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have taken many beatings over the years, both on the field and in the media. Regardless of who is manning the sidelines or taking snaps under center, the franchise usually ends up serving as a punching bag, or a punchline, or a get-right game. Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and current NBC NFL analyst Mike Tomlin dropped a JuJu Smith-Schuster quote during a recap of Cleveland 's 34-10 Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , and it perfectly sums up how the public views this football operation. "The Browns is the Browns." Todd Monken resented the assumption.

The first-year NFL HC oozed passion and intensity after his team earned a surprise 23-19 road victory versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . "The Browns are gonna Browns! F*** that!" he said in the postgame press conference. "The guys took that to heart."

Tomlin did not seem to take any offense , only expressing gratitude that he could now ignite a team without facing the ramifications on the gridiron. Monken admitted that he got caught up in the moment .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"First of all, I have a ton of respect for Mike Tomlin ," he told "The Pat McAfee Show" on Friday. "I hope to have the career that he's had as a head coach. And the only way you kill a narrative is to play better and to coach better. I tell our players {that}. It just happened they got me on a little roll.

"In that moment, I was just fired up, because in a lot of ways, you are that until you prove it wrong…. I really didn't have that planned. And now I told the guys, 'we got to continue to play good, dudes. I put that out there. I backed myself into a corner now.'"

Monken's frustration was understandable. He had only spent one year with Cleveland before eventually becoming the head coach. Dismissing the Browns because of their history discredits the potential value he can bring to the organization. Though, in fairness to Tomlin and any other skeptics, the team provided no evidence for growth after getting demolished by the Jags. What were people supposed to think?

Clearly, ensuing embarrassment left a mark on the locker room, and that might be the best thing Monken could have asked for going into Tampa . Deshaun Watson enjoyed one of his best Browns performances , the defense came through when it mattered most and Cleveland left Raymond James Stadium with a 1-1 record and a whole lot of vigor.

Now, the AFC North squad must prove it can repeat the triumphant effort in Sunday's home opener versus the Carolina Panthers (1-1). Todd Monken said it himself. Only tangible results can end negative narratives. They will look to produce those in Huntington Bank Field, and if successful, fans should prepare for another electrically charged press conference.

articles.title: ‘He Is Scary Bad’ — Skip Bayless Doesn’t Believe Arch Manning Inherited Eli and Peyton’s Talent
articles.summary: Arch Manning has been catching headlines ever since he entered his college career. There is no doubt that Manning is one of the most talented young quarterba...
articles.body:
Arch Manning has been catching headlines ever since he entered his college career. There is no doubt that Manning is one of the most talented young quarterbacks, but he has also been compared with some of the most recognizable names in the football world because of his famous family.

The attention around Manning will continue to increase, particularly as analysts examine his performances and expectations at Texas .

Skip Bayless Questions Arch Manning's Poise at Texas

In a recent episode of 'First Take', Skip Bayless shared his point of view on the young quarterback and weighed in on his upcoming game against Tennessee. He said:

"When I watch Arch Manning, he makes me nervous. I'm edge of seat for him. I root for him because I liked his uncles and I loved his grandfather, and he's next in line. And yet his accuracy comes and goes. When he's good, he's really good. He's a Manning. And when he's bad, which is more often than you would think it would be, he is scary bad. And for me, it started, Stephen A., when he blazed a new trail. He said, I'm not going to Tennessee where Peyton went, and I'm not going to Ole Miss where my grandfather and other uncle played."

I'm going to Texas. And I thought he had next at Texas, and he did not have next. Quinn Ewers came kept next. And for 2 years, he barely played. Arch barely played at Texas. And if you're that guy, that dude, that next Manning, you start from the start. And this is his first, you know, full year—last year, first full year of starting. And now he should be getting his legs underneath him. And for those first 3 quarters against Ohio State, it was scary bad. And then he sort of started to figure it out, got his legs underneath him. And regained his poise, which also comes and goes. And I watch him on the sideline, he gets down on himself, he hangs his head. I don't see the poise that a Manning should have consistently. And so, do I trust him at Tennessee? Texas is way better than Tennessee.

Arch is playing behind the best line in college football. He's got the most dynamic receiver duo in college football. Football in Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, and he's, he's got a defense that features a top 5 edge rusher. They, they should beat Tennessee. They're pretty heavily favored to beat Tennessee, but I just don't trust Arch to consistently play at the level I would expect, maybe unfairly so, from a Manning."

Manning comes with a famous surname, and all eyes will be on him as he continues his development at Texas. Fans and analysts will be excited to see how he performs against Tennessee, particularly with the expectations surrounding him. His family name has already placed considerable attention on his college career, and every performance gives analysts another opportunity to evaluate whether he can live up to those expectations.

articles.title: Game 160: Rangers at Twins
articles.summary: The Rangers come to town and we learn about a Ranger statue put up this year at Globe Life Park.
articles.body:
Well, what we all wanted is for the Twins to be playing meaningful baseball in September, right? And they are! It's just not meaningful for the Twins. Texas is currently tied with Houston for the one remaining AL playoff spot. The Astros have the tie-breaker; thanks to Rob Manfred, there'll be no more of those boring Game 163s. Veteran Jacob deGrom starts for Texas. Him being a little down this year at age 38 still means an ERA of 3.86 (and a FIP of 3.11; he strikes out 11.12 per nine innings). He throws an upper-90s fastball that still averages 97; he gets you with his slider.

Last year, I think I wrapped up by doing a quick rundown of all the teams currently seeking oodles of public money for brand new buildings, "renovations" to existing buildings (more luxury sections), massive tax giveaways for nearby land development, and the like. So, here's the 2026 version (set to the tune of Malvina Reynolds's " Little Boxes "):

There's the Guardians , and the White Sox and naturally the Vegas team Royals likely get two billion and the Cards want some of that

Rays also get TWO billion while a pol quotes Shel Silverstein there's all kinds of expansion plans don't forget the Timberwolves

It's a shorter list than last year, but that's largely because several teams already got their funny money!

That Rays one is really wild (all those links are to posts on Neil deMause's Field of Schemes website ). One of the county commissioners who voted to give away oodles outta taxpayer money said he got the idea from his daughter reading The Giving Tree :

"I have a 12-year-old daughter, when she was very young, I used to read her this book called The Giving Tree . If anyone has a child, you know what that book is about: You have a seed, and you let it grow, and it gives back over time, and it does all these things. And in a way, this park is like the Giving Tree."

Umm… the story is about a boy who finds a fruit tree, and takes from it and takes from it and takes from it over the years, and gives the tree NOTHING in return, and each time the boy/man takes, "the tree was very happy." Finally the man cuts the tree down just because he wanna, and "the tree was very happy." It's a deeply sad book written by a really weird man! Who traumatized kids with this cover:

Unless the commissioner meant how the public would keep giving and giving and get ZERO overall economic benefit from building a stadium, in which case that commissioner is smarter than most! (He is not.)

The Rangers won't be demanding a new building for another decade or so, since they just got their second since 1994. They'll of course want "renovation" money, it's only natural.

Some renovations/decorations the team is happy to pay for/ provide itself. This March, while the team was in spring training in Arizona, the team unveiled a decorative stadium statue called "One Riot, One Ranger." As Sam Blum of The Athletic explains , the title refers to a mostly phony-baloney legend of a 1896 incident where a single Texas Ranger stopped an illegal prizefight. The statue was finished by artist Waldine Tauch in 1961, and donated to the Love Field airport in Dallas. It was taken down by the airport in 2020, after a book came out about some of the less savory incidents in Ranger history.

Now, despite what the Rangers (the team) claimed when they issued a press release about moving the statue to Globe Life Field, the statue made in 1961 did not depict a generic Ranger. It was specifically modeled after one Jay Banks, who posed for it. (Davy Andrews at FanGraphs has the details, in a thorough post that The Athletic draws on.)

Jay Banks became quite famous for a picture that appeared in Life magazine in 1956. Here it is from The Athletic article, slightly altered by me:

The squiggly blob obscures what was in the original photo: an effigy of a person being hung. The casual gentleman on the left is Jay Banks. He was there to make sure the school would NOT be integrated. (You can see the original at either the Fangraphs link or The Athletic one, if you must.)

Yeah, if that's the photo the guy was famous for, I wouldn't mention him in the press release about his statue, either!

Naturally, some people were upset by this, but since they weren't the richest luxury-box season-ticket holders, the team didn't care.

Ah, taxpayer-funded stadiums and their decorative delights, folks. What won't they think of next? Well, we've got all offseason to find out!

articles.title: Internationals take 7-3 Presidents Cup lead after foursomes sweep
articles.summary: The Internationals completed a sensational foursomes clean sweep Friday to surge into a commanding 7-3 lead over the United States at the Presidents Cup.The...
articles.body:
The Internationals completed a sensational foursomes clean sweep Friday to surge into a commanding 7-3 lead over the United States at the Presidents Cup.

Trailing 3-2 after Thursday's opening four-ball matches, the Internationals won all five of day two's foursomes to open up a four-point cushion heading into the weekend at Medinah Country Club.

Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor produced one of the most notable victories, taking down world number one Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns 1-up in a tense battle.

The Canadians edged into the lead on the 12th hole when Conners drilled his second shot to six feet for Taylor to tap in a birdie.

Taylor then made sure of victory on the 18th with an extraordinary approach shot from the fairway that finished just two feet from the hole for an easy par.

Burns had a chance to square the match but his 17-foot birdie putt curled agonizingly around the cup as the Internationals claimed the win.

Earlier, Japan's Hideki Matsuyama and South Korea's Im Sung-jae partnered to get the first point of the day with a 3&2 defeat of Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman.

Former Masters champion Matsuyama rolled in a 19-foot par putt to clinch victory on the 16th.

New Zealand's Ryan Fox and Australia's Min Woo Lee dug deep to win a nervy duel with Collin Morikawa and Windham Clark 1-up to add another Internationals point.

The sweep was completed with Adam Scott and Christiaan Bezuidenhout scoring a 3&2 defeat of Justin Thomas and Cameron Young before Tom Kim and Kim Si-woo downed Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele 4&3.

The win was only the third time the Internationals have swept a session since the Presidents Cup was first held in 1994.

They are attempting to win the biennial team golf tournament for the first time since 1998 while the United States are chasing an 11th-straight victory in the Ryder Cup-style event.

"We just wanted to come out and win the session," International captain Geoff Ogilvy said afterwards.

"The guys were all in a great frame of mind, but you never imagine going five zip...but we've seen it in these events when you get some momentum, it inspires all the groups," he said.

United States captain Brandt Snedeker paid tribute to the rivals' performance, but insisted there was still all to play for with 20 points up for grabs over the weekend.

"Hats off to the International team," Snedeker said. "They went out there and played great and made a ton of putts.

"I feel terrible for our guys -- they grinded out there and it just wasn't meant to be. But that being said, there's still 20 points out there. There's still a lot of golf here left to play," the captain added.

"I've said it all week -- we have high-quality, high-character guys. They are fierce competitors. We're going to kind of wash this off on the way home tonight.

The United States has a 13-1-1 edge against the Internationals.
